screening_results.reason: This is an empirical human fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that included a visual cue component (words “Alcohol”/“Water”) alongside taste delivery (multimodal), and used an explicit within-participant contrast (Alcohol > Water). The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain activation clusters for the Alcohol>Water contrast, e.g., ACC and thalamus) and also extracted ROI contrast estimates (ventral striatum) for analysis, satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise result. Participant demographics, cue type, and preprocessing/statistics details are provided or noted as available in Supplementary Materials. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual cocaine pictures (drug-related visual stimuli). It reports a within-participant contrast (cocaine > neutral) and presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results with familywise-error corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activations. Methods include MRI field strength, preprocessing, and statistical software details. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for visual cue-related task-evoked voxelwise analyses. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug and neutral video stimuli, so I3 is met. However, the full text reports only behavioral/subjective craving results and does not report any task-evoked voxelwise fMRI results (no within-participant drug-cue > control contrast results, no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical maps or coordinate tables). Therefore it does not meet I4 (at least one within-participant cue>control contrast) or I5 (qualifying group-level voxelwise result). The full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet mandatory imaging-analysis inclusion criteria (I4 and I5).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts of cocaine cues > neutral control stimuli (cocaine minus neutral), and conducts group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM8) with cluster correction; results are reported as tables/figures with MNI coordinates. Key methodological details (3.0T MRI, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8, participant sex counts, cue type) are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and includes qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The full text is complete and reports fMRI group-level voxelwise results, but it does NOT report a within-participant voxelwise contrast of drug cues>control stimuli (e.g., alcohol>neutral/food) required by I4. The imaging results focus on regulation contrasts ([LATER>NOW] and [REAPPRAISE-Negative>LOOK-Negative]) and parametric modulation by craving; behavioral ratings show alcohol>food effects, but no group-level alcohol>control voxelwise contrast or coordinates are reported. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I4 and cannot be included in this cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Included criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual alcohol cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported for regulation contrasts), I6 (results reported in tables/figures), I7 (methods report cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria from the list are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study presenting a visual cannabis cue-reactivity task in adolescent regular users. It includes a within-participant contrast of cannabis > non-cannabis cues, reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected statistical thresholds, and provides requisite methodological details (age/sex, 3T field strength, preprocessing and FSL/FEAT software, acquisition parameters). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual cue fMRI, within-subject cue>control contrast, whole-brain voxelwise results, adequate reporting). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related and neutral images (visual cue paradigm) and reports within-subject contrasts (BOLD_drugcues > BOLD_neutral) at the group level. Voxelwise analyses were performed (whole-brain and an OFC mask small-volume approach) with FWE-corrected results reported, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Methods report participant demographics, cue type, 3T scanner, and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants (heavy social drinkers) using pictorial alcohol vs neutral cues (visual stimuli) and a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (FWE-corrected whole-brain decreases by oxytocin vs placebo; coordinates and table provided), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise statistical results. Participant age/sex and cue type are reported; further MRI/method details are indicated in Supplementary Information. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study is a PET molecular imaging study measuring dopamine release with [18F]fallypride in cocaine-dependent participants, not an fMRI study. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI with visual cue component) not satisfied — modality is PET, not fMRI; I4 (within-participant fMRI contrast drug cues>control) not satisfied — while the study uses drug vs neutral cue conditions, the measurement is PET binding potential, not task-evoked BOLD fMRI contrasts; I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked fMRI results, whole-brain or SVC) not satisfied — no voxelwise fMRI statistical maps are reported. The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E6) apply specifically to this manuscript, but failure to meet the required inclusion criteria mandates exclusion.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual cocaine pictures vs neutral pictures (visual cues). It reports within-participant contrasts (cocaine > neutral) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain cluster-corrected results and a small-volume-corrected PAG result). Results and coordinates are reported in the main text/supplement; methods report participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it does not assess cue-reactivity using a clear visual cue component. The paradigm used taste (alcohol vs juice) as the primary cues (alcohol taste delivery), although within-participant alcohol>juice contrasts (I4) are present. The study does provide group-level voxelwise task-evoked results/maps consistent with whole-brain reporting (I5), and reporting details such as participant sex/age, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software are present (I6, I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no clear visual cue component). Full text appears complete. Confidence=0.90.

This is an empirical task-activated fMRI study that used visually presented drug-related word cues (alcohol and cannabis) in an addiction-Stroop paradigm, meeting the review objective. The study reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol>color and cannabis>color) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level correction (3dClustSim). Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing adequate extraction of qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study investigates smoking cue reactivity using visual smoking vs neutral images (meets I3 and I4) and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength, and preprocessing software (meets I7). However, the cue-reactivity results are reported as beta weights extracted from a priori ROIs (four insula subregions and two ACC ROIs) rather than as group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). No qualifying whole-brain or SVC task contrast (drug cues > control) is reported or indicated as available in the main text or supplements. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only task results with no qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. Exclusion IDs met: E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (craving and aversion pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (Cr vs mosaic; Av vs mosaic) and group-level random-effects voxelwise GLM results with FDR correction, describing brain coordinates/regions and statistical thresholds. The methods include MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and analysis software (Brain Voyager), participant sex/age description (male, age-matched groups), and cue types. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI task-evoked voxelwise results and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-cue videotapes (cocaine cues) and control/emotional tapes, satisfying the review scope. It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts comparing cocaine-cue viewing to baseline and to sad/happy cue conditions (emotion0 vs baseline1, emotion1 vs emotion0, emotion2 vs baseline2), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results using voxelwise t maps and randomization-based p values (whole-brain voxelwise results presented in figures/tables). Necessary methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T MRI, SPM96 preprocessing/statistics). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (120 food pictures) and scrambled control images, employing within-subject contrasts (food > control) across nicotine/placebo sessions. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain analyses with PFWE values and coordinate tables; small-volume/ROI analyses also reported), with preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), MRI field strength (3T), and participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) provided. Therefore it meets all meta-analysis inclusion requirements for visual cue-based natural reward fMRI studies. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes task-evoked voxelwise results; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts; is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports only ROI-based task-evoked fMRI results (percent signal change in individualized PFC/ACC ROIs) and group-level statistics on those ROI measures; it does not provide a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked contrast (drug cue > control) in the main text or tables. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (drug cue-reactivity with clear visual cues), I4 (within-participant smoke>rest contrasts used to compute PSC), I7 (reporting of participants, cue type, 3 T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC task-evoked statistical result is reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded under E3.

This article is a narrative synthesis/review of a series of neuroimaging (ERP and fMRI) studies rather than a single empirical fMRI paper reporting new group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. The full text does not present original within-participant fMRI cue>control voxelwise contrasts (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) with coordinates or statistical maps required for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review) and does not satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, or I5.

This is an fMRI study that used visual marketing clips (alcohol, cannabis, neutral) as cues and performed within-subject contrasts (cannabis marketing > neutral; alcohol marketing > neutral) at the individual level and group-level GLM second-level analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-level FWE correction reported; clusters referenced in Supporting Information Table S1 and Table 2) and ROI analyses were also conducted. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual cue-based fMRI cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise results (including supplementary tables). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual anticipatory cues (circle/square/triangle) signaling monetary reward/loss (natural rewards). It reports within-participant contrasts Reward Cue–Neutral Cue and Loss Cue–Neutral Cue and performs group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME) with cluster-correction (pcorrected < .05) for at least the Loss Cue–Neutral Cue contrast. Voxelwise ROI analyses and tables/figures of results are provided. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), task details, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a visual alcohol cue reactivity paradigm with explicit Alcohol > Control within-participant contrasts reported. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain GLM results are presented (cluster FWE-corrected, voxelwise threshold p<.001) with MNI coordinates, tables and figures. The manuscript reports participant demographics, cue type (visual alcohol images), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Therefore all inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This fMRI study used visual drug-cue videos (heroin video) and performed within-subject drug cue > neutral contrasts (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the reported analyses are ROI-based: mean contrast estimates were extracted from a priori spherical ROIs and entered into ANOVAs and correlations. The manuscript does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected (SVC) statistical results (no SPM voxelwise maps or SVC-corrected coordinates are presented), i.e. no qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result is available. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying voxelwise outcome). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise group-level task-evoked result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Due to the absence of qualifying voxelwise results, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports within-subject Smoking>Neutral contrasts and conducts whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses using FSL/FLAME with cluster correction (Pcorrected < .05; cluster-defining threshold z=3.1), and presents significant clusters (tables/figures). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies with qualifying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an fMRI study using visual video cues (cocaine, gambling, sad) and reports within-participant contrasts (V1>B1 and V2>B2 for each video type) and post-hoc within-subject comparisons of cocaine videos > sad/gambling videos in participant groups. Results are reported as group-level voxelwise analyses with whole-brain family-wise-error correction (FWE P<0.05) and presented in tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type, 3T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, AFNI, BioImage Suite) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials referenced but not required. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (videos of drug and food), providing within-participant contrasts (DRUG > FOOD) and group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain thresholds and small-volume-corrected ROIs. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Results are presented as voxelwise group analyses and coordinate-based findings. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

The study is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task using visual alcohol pictures (I3 met). It used a within-subject alcohol vs neutral design and conducted within-participant analyses (I4 met) and reports participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI, and preprocessing/software (I7 met). However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Instead, results are ROI-to-ROI PPI/seed-based connectivity analyses and ROI-based findings only. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria for connectivity/ROI-only studies (E4) and ROI-only reporting with no qualifying voxelwise result (E3). Inclusion criterion I5 (requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise group-level task-evoked result) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of natural reward (favorite-food) cue-reactivity that used personalized guided-imagery audiotaped scripts (not visual stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts of favorite-food vs control/neutral conditions are reported), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with FWE/correction are reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/supplement), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (requires a clear visual cue component; this study used auditory guided imagery and no visual-only or visual-containing cues). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails to meet I3 (visual cue requirement) necessary for this meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity.

This is an rtfMRI neurofeedback study using visual smoking cues (satisfies I3). However, the imaging analyses are ROI-based percent BOLD change comparisons (downregulation vs baseline) and paired t-tests on extracted ROI signals; the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrast of drug cues > control stimuli nor whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Therefore it fails I4 and I5. According to exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise results), this study should be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photographs). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues (smokers’ smoking vs neutral blocks) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses with reported t-values and cluster thresholds). The paper provides necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing and SPM5/MATLAB software). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs neutral pictures), with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (factorial whole-brain interaction, FWE correction via permutation-derived cluster thresholds). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/analysis software (SPM8/12), and include tables/figures of results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-evoked, task-based voxelwise fMRI results relevant to drug cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI task study using visual cues (picture-based cocaine and food cue tasks), with within-participant contrasts (cocaine>neutral and food>neutral) and group-level voxelwise results reported. The paper reports whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected results and small-volume-corrected hypothalamus results (voxel P<0.001 with cluster P<0.05 FWE or SVC), meeting the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked statistical outcomes. Participant demographics, cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM) are described. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it lacks a clear visual cue component. The task used individualized audiotaped guided-imagery scripts (auditory-only) to evoke craving/stress; although participants imagined visual content, no visual stimuli or multimodal (including visual) cues were presented. The study does meet I4 (within-participant favorite-food > neutral contrasts), I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, including small-volume-corrected findings in the basolateral amygdala. The methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, MATLAB), participant demographics (female, ages 18–35), and detailed imaging/analysis procedures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical design).

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject cue>neutral contrasts (smoking cue minus neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (condition by NMR group ANOVA) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction, and reports cluster results and extracted percent signal changes. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FILM) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cues (images) and a within-subject contrast of smoking versus neutral images. Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (searchlight MVPA accuracy maps warped to MNI space, smoothed, and tested with nonparametric methods and cluster-wise correction for multiple comparisons), with results reported as significant clusters/regions. Participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI, FSL, Princeton MVPA toolbox) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual (and tactile) cannabis cues, so it meets I3. It also performed within-subject contrasts of cannabis vs neutral cues within its PPI connectivity analyses, satisfying I4. However, the paper does not report any qualifying task-evoked voxelwise activation contrasts (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) of drug cues > control stimuli; instead the main reported results are seed-based connectivity (PPI) and Granger effective-connectivity analyses. According to exclusion criterion E4 (studies that report only seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity without also reporting a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result), this study must be excluded. Inclusion I5 (a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation result) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol and control images (visual component present). The paper reports a within-subject contrast comparing alcohol versus control conditions (CRAlcohol - CRControl) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with family-wise error correction; results are reported in tables and figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with a within-participant contrast of food>non-food. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected, Z>2.3, p<.05) presented in figures and tables. Key details required by I7 are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software (FSL)). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) to probe cue-reactivity and neurofeedback effects. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > rest/control and uses group-level voxelwise statistical analyses: FWE-corrected whole-brain results (right inferior frontal gyrus) and small-volume-corrected ROI results in the ventral striatum, with peak MNI coordinates provided. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, Turbo-BrainVoyager) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study examines visual food-cue reactivity in women with bulimia nervosa and includes within-subject contrasts of food cues > neutral cues (satisfies I3 and I4) and reports participant demographics and MRI parameters (I7). However, all reported neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based (average ROI signal comparisons and paired t-tests), with no evidence in the main text of group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC-corrected result). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (qualifying whole-brain or SVC-corrected voxelwise result). I6 is not satisfied because no qualifying voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and explicit within-subject contrasts. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., ADMIT_TASTY>ADMIT_NOT_TASTY, ADMIT_TASTY>REGULATE_TASTY, REGULATE_TASTY>ADMIT_TASTY) and second-level, group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (voxelwise P<0.001 with cluster-level FWE correction) with peak coordinates and figures. Imaging parameters (3T scanner), preprocessing (SPM8), and participant demographics (age/sex: healthy adult women) are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages). It reports a within-participant contrast of alcoholic vs. non-alcoholic beverages and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (t-contrasts and conjunction analyses) with peak-level statistics and coordinates (tables, pFWE/puncorrected thresholds) and region-level small-volume/mask-restricted corrections. Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity voxelwise results suitable for meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis cues (images) and reports within-participant contrasts (cannabis > neutral). The paper presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses: exploratory ROI voxelwise analyses using FLAME produced a significant cluster in the left putamen with MNI coordinates (i.e., a small-volume/ROI-corrected voxelwise result). Methods report participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Results suitable for meta-analysis (coordinate reported).

The study is an original task-based fMRI study with within-subject cue>control contrasts (gain cue > neutral cue, loss cue > neutral cue) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction. However, it does not examine drug-related cues (e.g., alcohol images) or natural reward-related cues (e.g., erotic or other primary reward images). Instead, it uses a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with monetary cues (secondary reinforcers). Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a visual cue component) is not met. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts present), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with SVC reported), I6 (results available in main/supplementary materials), I7 (participant sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software reported; MRI field strength likely in appendix but missing would not alone exclude). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI task using visual alcohol-associated cues (pictures) and an explicit within-participant contrast of alcohol-associated > abstract (control) stimuli. The methods describe voxelwise, group-level GLM analysis (SPM99) with smoothing and group fixed-effects inference and report activations in reward and attention networks, satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. The paper provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (50 alcohol pictures vs 50 neutral pictures) with a within-subject contrast Alcohol>Neutral. Group-level voxelwise results are reported: Alcohol>Neutral contrast images entered into second-level random-effects analyses; significant activations survived small-volume FWE-correction within a priori striatal ROIs (ventral striatum and putamen), and whole-brain exploratory results are also presented. MRI field strength (3T Philips), preprocessing and stats software (SPM8) and participant characteristics are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only-only, no connectivity-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrast, is empirical).

This is an event-related task fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and neutral visual controls, with within-subject drug>neutral contrasts and group-level voxelwise analyses. Methods report preprocessing and SPM8 regression, subject-level contrasts and random-effects second-level voxelwise t-tests with AlphaSim correction (whole-brain voxelwise thresholding). Participant demographics and MRI field strength (3.0 T) are reported. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cues), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results, AlphaSim-corrected), I6 (results reported in main text/ROIs with peak coordinates referenced), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study uses an fMRI cannabis cue-exposure task with visual components (images) and reports a within-participant cannabis cue > appetitive cue contrast, and reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition details. However, the paper reports ROI-based mean z-statistics extracted from predefined anatomical masks rather than presenting group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected coordinates/tables/figures). Therefore it does not meet the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise group-level result (I5). Exclusion is based on E3 (only ROI analyses without qualifying voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (70 food images vs 70 non-food images) and a within-subjects placebo/insulin design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) and task-evoked, group-level voxelwise results with family-wise-error correction and small-volume ROI correction (NAc, VTA) and provides peak coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM12, GLM denoise) and analysis software are reported. Results include whole-brain and small-volume-corrected voxelwise findings and coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (pleasant, unpleasant, neutral, cigarette-related) and assesses cue-reactivity in smokers planning to quit. The study includes within-subject contrasts (cigarette-related, pleasant, unpleasant vs neutral) analyzed with whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects GLMs (FDR q<.01) and reports voxelwise results in figures and tables with Talairach coordinates. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI acquisition parameters, preprocessing (BrainVoyager), and statistical software are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos (e-cigarette vs electronic toothbrush) in experienced e-cigarette users. It includes within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette cues > neutral cues and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from a random-effects GLM with voxelwise maps corrected via a Monte-Carlo cluster-level procedure; Talairach coordinates and cluster results are reported. The paper provides MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX), cue type, and participant information. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and explicitly states that a voxelwise approach was not completed, thus meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cannabis cue-reactivity task) and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear within-participant drug-cue > control within-subject contrast is reported) and I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used an fMRI monetary reward-anticipation task with visual cues (arrow indicators), providing a within-subject contrast of monetary reward > verbal feedback. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction and coordinate peaks (e.g., nucleus accumbens, DLPFC), and includes methodological details (3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing/analysis) and participant demographics. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for non-drug (natural) reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and reports qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cocaine-related cues (cocaine pictures) vs natural scene control pictures with a within-participant contrast (cocaine>natural). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses are reported (whole-brain inference: height threshold Z>3 and cluster probability p<.05, corrected for whole-brain multiple comparisons), with VBM and fMRI voxelwise results and seed coordinates (MNI) provided. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Given these facts, the study meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visually presented geometric stimuli paired with alcohol (drug-related cues). It reports a within-subject contrast [CS+ > CS−] (drug-paired cues > control cues) at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain inference (cluster-level FWE correction, cluster-forming p<0.001), with peak coordinates reported in tables and figures. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8, FSL steps), and participant demographics. Thus all inclusion criteria for the review are met, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, supplementary materials referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (500-ms images) with within-subject contrasts (cocaine > neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports ROI-based and whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise results (tables/figures) and provides necessary methodological details (participant demographics, cue types, 3T scanner, preprocessing with SPM8, statistical software). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion is due to mismatch with the meta-analysis scope: the study used PET imaging ([15O]H2O PET) and script-guided auditory mental imagery rather than functional MRI with a clear visual cue component. While the paper provides a within-participant cue>control contrast (cocaine imagery vs neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (SPM voxelwise analyses with coordinate tables/figures), it does not meet the required modality or visual-cue inclusion criterion. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (within-participant drug cues>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported in figures/tables/coordinates), I7 (participant and methods details reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (Functional MRI study with a clear visual cue component). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis and cigarette images (visual cues). Within-participant contrasts of interest are reported (Can > Neutral and Can > Neutral + Cigarette). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain 2x2 ANOVAs with FEAT, cluster-wise correction Z>2.3, cluster p<.05). Demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (fMRIPrep, FSL/FEAT) are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (infant faces) probing a natural (social/caregiving) reward (baby schema). Within-subject contrasts were tested (baby faces vs fixation and High vs Low baby schema), and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (z-thresholding and cluster FWE correction) with cluster peaks in ventral striatum. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (palatable food images) and a within-participant contrast (food > nonfood). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (one-sample t-tests and whole-brain multiple regression with cluster-level FWE correction) with coordinates and figures, and provides MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical details (3T, SPM12). Thus it meets all stated inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material not required for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual word cues (alcohol-related vs neutral words), with within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses reported across the whole brain (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds described). Participant demographics and scanning/preprocessing details are provided and the manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of cue-induced cocaine craving using audiovisual (visual+auditory) stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts between cocaine-cue and neutral segments; however, the analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) based (percent signal change and fraction of pixels exceeding an arbitrary correlation threshold in preselected neuroanatomic regions) rather than group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected maps. No qualifying voxelwise SPM-style results or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistics are presented, so it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity with a within-subject alcohol>water (drug cue>control) contrast and whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise results. Although primary stimulus modality is gustatory (taste), the task includes an explicit visual cue component (visual presentation of “Alcohol Taste”/“Control Taste”) making it a multimodal design that includes visual cues. The paper reports whole-brain cluster-corrected analyses with tables of peak coordinates, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using visual smoking cues (grayscale images). It used a within-subject CUE>neutral contrast (abstinence vs satiety sessions) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with multiple-comparison correction and cluster masking; coordinates/figures/tables are provided. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (FSL), and participant age/sex. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore the article satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (grayscaled images) alongside haptic cues. The study reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., VS–VC, HS–HC, HS–VS) and group-level whole-brain RFX-GLM/ANOVA voxelwise analyses with cluster-size multiple-comparisons correction. Statistical maps and peak coordinates are reported in text/tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual film cues (cocaine, sex, nature) that assesses cue-induced craving. It includes within-subject contrasts (cocaine film > nature film) and group-level voxelwise, task-evoked statistical analyses (one-sample and two-sample t tests with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster extent) reported across the whole brain and summarized in tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI v2.2) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues in participants on methadone maintenance. The study reports a within-participant contrast (heroin-related > neutral) with group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (t-maps, table of coordinates; p<.0001, cluster-level corrected at whole-brain analysis). Core methods and results are present (introduction, methods, results, discussion), and necessary metadata are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing with SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related vs neutral images). It includes within-subject contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) at the group level, using whole-brain random-effects voxelwise GLM with cluster-size correction; results are reported with corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. Participant details (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (Alcohol Pictures Task) with college students. It reports within-participant alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage contrasts and group-level voxelwise whole-brain ANOVA results with cluster-wise whole-brain correction (clusters >2619 µl, voxel-wise F(2,40)>3.23, p<.05, whole-brain corrected p<.05) and cluster coordinates in Table 3. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), preprocessing (SPM5) and group analysis in AFNI. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked cue>control results and contains sufficient methodological detail. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, lacking within-participant cue>control contrast, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol images in recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients. It includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (one-sample t-test and multiple regression) with correction for multiple comparisons (AlphaSim-derived cluster extent corresponding to PFWE < 0.05). Results are presented in tables and figures (e.g., Table 2a, Table 3, Figures 1–3), and the manuscript provides participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (visual alcohol vs neutral images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5/SPM8). All required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol-related images (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage images) with a within-participant contrast (alcohol>non-alcohol) at the group level. The manuscript reports voxelwise task-evoked results (one-sample t-test, voxel-level analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster reporting) and provides figures/tables of activations. fMRI acquisition (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 are described. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise statistical reporting. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (cigarette video cues) and a multimodal alcohol taste paradigm (with visual cue labels). The authors computed within-participant contrasts (Cigarette Cues > Control Cues and Alcohol Cues > Control Cues) and ran whole-brain GLMs (38 whole-brain GLMs reported) to identify peak voxels; group-level voxelwise analyses were used to define ROIs (leave-one-out procedure) and voxelwise results/coordinates are described. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smokers using videotaped visual cues (visual-only/multimodal including visual component) and reports within-subject contrasts (cigarette cue crave > neutral; cigarette cue resist > neutral; and direct contrasts crave vs resist). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed with FSL/FEAT and cluster correction (Z>2.3, p<.01) and reported anatomical results; participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical perfusion fMRI study of cigarette cue reactivity using audio-visual (visual) smoking cues, with a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > nonsmoking control cues. Group-level voxelwise SPM analyses are reported (both unmasked whole-brain cluster results and small-volume-corrected ROI results) with coordinates and statistical maps; craving–activation correlations are reported at corrected thresholds. Participant demographics, cue type, field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual anticipatory cues (shapes) signaling monetary rewards/losses (natural reward). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of reward-cue > non-incentive cue (anticipation) and outcome contrasts, and group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-based correction (voxelwise ANOVA, reported suprathreshold clusters). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics (AFNI). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (results clearly available in main text/tables/figures), and I7 (reported participant and imaging details). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos (cocaine and food) and continuous craving ratings. It includes within-participant contrasts isolating cocaine video effects relative to food (hierarchical regression and direct cocaine>food comparisons) and reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses with cluster correction and ROI-corrected connectivity analyses). Results (activation maps and coordinates) are described in the main text and supplementary material is referenced. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and neutral images (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of heroin-related > neutral cues and relevant one-sample and two-sample group-level voxelwise t-tests (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain family-wise error correction (p≤0.05) and anatomical loci (I5,I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM5) are reported (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This full text is an empirical fMRI study of favorite-food cue reactivity (natural reward) with whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts for favorite-food cues vs control/other conditions are reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with correction are reported), I6 (voxelwise results are described and available in main/supplementary materials), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, and analysis software details reported). However, it fails I3: the cue modality is guided-imagery audiotapes (auditory/personalized imagery), not visual or multimodal designs that include visual cues. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not include a clear visual cue component required by the review.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related and pleasant cues (CSD+, CSP+) and neutral control images, meeting the visual cue requirement. The authors report within-participant contrasts (CSD+ vs CS− and CSP+ vs CS−) as primary neural measures. The paper includes group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (referenced in Tables S1–S2 and Figures S3–S4) and ROI analyses; voxelwise results are reported in supplementary materials, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Key methodological details (participants, MRI field strength=4T, preprocessing/statistical software=S﻿PM8, cue types) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (validated smoking images). The methods report within-subject contrasts (‘Smoking > neutral’) and entry of individual contrast maps into group-level voxelwise analyses (2-sample t-test and fixed-effect GLM). Results are reported as voxelwise task-evoked activations with cluster-level thresholds and detailed tables of significant clusters (MNI coordinates, BA, cluster sizes) referenced in the text. MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, MATLAB) are reported; participant age/sex and cue type are provided. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions). Although the sample is small (N=5 smokers), that affects study weight but not eligibility for inclusion per the review criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol-associated cues with healthy controls and abstinent alcoholics. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol-related > control stimuli (visual neutral and scrambled) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction (threshold P<0.05 corrected) in predefined ROIs including striatum, ACC and mPFC; coordinates and tables/figures of activation are provided. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (visual), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (WATCH Food > WATCH Neutral) reported as voxelwise group-level results (activation maps, thresholding, and MNI coordinates). Methods report scanner field strength (3T), SPM8 preprocessing/statistics, participant age/sex, and cue type. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of opioid cue-reactivity using an opioid-word Stroop task (visual word cues). It reports within-participant contrasts of opioid words versus neutral words (OW minus NW) and conducts group-level voxelwise SPM12 second-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results, satisfying the requirement for a task-evoked voxelwise result. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM12, AFNI steps), and participant demographics/age range. Although the paper also reports DCM effective connectivity results, it includes the requisite voxelwise activation analyses, so it is eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of visual drug-cue reactivity.

This is an fMRI study of smokers using visual cues (personal and standard smoking vs nonsmoking environments and proximal cues). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>nonsmoking stimuli (e.g., PSEs vs PNEs and smoking vs nonsmoking proximal cues) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected threshold z=3.1, p<0.05) identifying activation clusters (insula, striatum, parietal cortex, etc.). Results (including supplementary tables/figures) provide voxelwise task-evoked statistical findings. Methods report participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues vs control images, reporting whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (RFX ANOVA and RFX ANCOVA) with the within-participant contrast 'smoke > control' and corrected maps and coordinate tables. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software (BrainVoyager) are reported. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-evoked visual cue-reactivity (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (methamphetamine, sexual, neutral images) with within-participant contrasts (methamphetamine>neutral; sexual>neutral) reported. The paper includes group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected results with peak coordinates and cluster size reported for the left superior frontal cortex) and ROI analyses; voxelwise results are reported in the main text with coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a study protocol/RCT planning fMRI cue-reactivity and rtfMRI neurofeedback using visual alcohol cues, but it does not report any original task-evoked voxelwise fMRI results. Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI study with visual alcohol cues). Inclusion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast results are presented) and I5 (no group-level whole-brain or SVC voxelwise task-evoked results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical/paper without original human fMRI data reported). Full text appears complete as a protocol, but contains no empirical results, so study must be excluded from a meta-analysis requiring task-evoked voxelwise results.

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity that includes visual cues both alone (unisensory) and combined with odor (multisensory), directly addressing the review objective. The study reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (CIG-I > NEU-I) under odorless and cigarette-odor conditions. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected, Z>2.3, p<0.05), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise results. Results are presented in the main text and figures/tables; participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are all reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (shapes indicating effort and monetary reward) to probe neural responses to a natural reward (monetary) anticipation/valuation task. The study reports within-participant event-related regressors for cue presentation and combined-group validation analyses showing ventral striatum and dACC activations (i.e., cue-related > baseline effects). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE-corrected clusters and tables of coordinates for cue and feedback contrasts, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise results. Participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details are reported or referenced (Table 1 and Methods). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual cocaine cue videotapes (clear visual component). The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing cocaine-cue viewing (first 30 s and full 3 min) to a neutral baseline and conducts group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain voxelwise correlations with TES and group-level voxelwise comparisons relapsers vs nonrelapsers), reporting cluster coordinates and significance thresholds. MRI field strength (1.5 T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical approaches are described. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and reporting of whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked results (coordinates and thresholds). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli tailored to cocaine, alcohol, and cigarette users. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral control images and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates and cluster-level correction (voxelwise threshold and AFNI 3dClustSim cluster correction). Methods report MRI field strength, preprocessing and analysis software (SPM12, AFNI), participant demographics, and task details. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using alcohol (drug) visual cues as distractors and includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol vs. neutral/scramble) and interaction contrasts. Group-level voxelwise second-level analyses were performed and reported using a voxel-wise threshold (p<0.001) with cluster-extent correction corresponding to pFWE<0.05; results are described in the main text and supplementary materials. Key methodological details (3T field strength, SPM8 preprocessing/statistics, cue type, participant demographics) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine-deprived smokers that used visual cigarette cues (images of cigarettes) and neutral object images, with within-subject contrasts comparing cigarette cues to control (e.g., acquaintance+cigarette vs acquaintance+pen). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo simulation, p<0.05 corrected) and peak coordinates/figures/ROI results are provided. Participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related and pleasant (IAPS) cues in abstinent opioid-dependent males and healthy controls. It reports within-subject contrasts (heroin vs. baseline/neutral; pleasant vs. baseline) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds (FDR-corrected; voxelwise results reported via coordinates). Relevant participant details (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using clearly presented visual cues (alcohol, food, neutral symbols) and reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues versus control stimuli (high-threat alcohol cues contrasted with high-threat food and neutral cues). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain analyses with cluster correction via AFNI 3dClustSim) and ROI analyses/small-volume approaches are also described. Voxelwise results are described in the main text and linked to figures/supplement. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, CONN) are reported. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the manuscript meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of active cocaine users using visual cocaine-related background pictures versus neutral backgrounds (visual cue component). The authors report within-participant contrasts comparing cocaine-related versus neutral backgrounds and interaction contrasts (high WM cocaine > high WM neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with voxelwise and cluster thresholds (t=4.14, p≤.001; cluster-size correction via Monte Carlo), and ROI analyses are additionally reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study that uses clear visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water), includes within-participant contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation/outcome/delivery, and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (one-sample t-tests, one-way ANOVAs, regression) with coordinate foci and multiple-comparison correction. Results and thresholds are reported in the text and supplemented via NeuroVault. Participant characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, ICA-AROMA) are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cannabis cues in cannabis-dependent adults. It includes within-participant contrasts (cannabis>Gaussian baseline, cannabis>nature, cannabis>food), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM5; voxelwise threshold and cluster extent, cluster tables/coordinates), and provides participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Thus all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied.

This is an empirical task-fMRI study using visual emotional images (IAPS) as natural reward/affective cues, with within-subject contrasts (positive>neutral and negative>neutral) modeled at first level and group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM8) with cluster correction reported. The paper reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software, and provides whole-brain voxelwise results in text/figures/tables. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual smoking and neutral images, with within-participant contrasts (smoking-related cues > neutral cues) reported. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are presented (cluster-thresholded Z>2.3, p<.05) with coordinates/tables and figures. Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual pictorial stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking-related > neutral cues at the group level and provides voxelwise task-evoked results with stereotactic coordinates and statistical thresholds (e.g., smoking vs. neutral, p<0.001 uncorrected; regression results reported with coordinates at p<0.005 uncorrected). Methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), participant age/sex, and cue type. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol stimuli (alcohol pictures vs neutral IAPS), with a within-participant contrast modeled as alcohol > neutral. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (voxel-wise thresholds, cluster-extent thresholds, tables/figures and supplement references), and provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study that includes clear visual stimuli (unimodal pictures and bimodal picture+odor trials). The manuscript reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., cannabis picture > flower picture; cannabis picture > baseline) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected z≥2.3, p<.05) as well as small-volume ROI analyses. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, AFNI, ANTS) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual-only stimuli (alcohol vs non-alcohol pictures) embedded in a visual oddball task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol distractors > non-alcohol distractors (AD vs NAD) and related AD-NAD contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported: whole-brain voxelwise rmANOVA with FWE-corrected clusters (left IPL, right dorsal ACC) and a priori amygdala small-volume ROI analyses (age-adjusted z-scores) with significance testing. Methods report participant age/group, MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, SPM5). These elements satisfy I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in heroin-dependent participants using audiovisual drug-related (visual component present) and matched neutral cues. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of heroin>neutral conditions and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise 2×2 ANOVA (cluster-corrected) with reported cluster locations/coordinates (tables/figures). Methods include MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (FSL/FEAT), and participant age/sex information. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol-related vs. neutral pictures (visual cues). It reports within-participant contrast images (alcohol > neutral) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM, AlphaSim cluster correction to pFWE < 0.05). Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrast, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task-evoked voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity used visual alcohol images and neutral beverage controls (I3).
