It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol>neutral beverage (I4) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level random effects, cluster-corrected within the striatum, with reported MNI coordinates and corrected p-values), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (I5, I6). The paper reports participant sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), addressing reporting preferences (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not limited to ROI-only results (E3), are task-evoked rather than connectivity/resting-state only (E4), include the required within-participant cue>control contrasts (not only between-group contrasts; E5), and are empirical human fMRI data (not a review; E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports task-based perfusion fMRI in human smokers using audiovisual smoking cues (visual component present). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > nonsmoking (cue vs control) at the group level, and reports voxelwise whole-brain statistical results with MNI coordinates, cluster thresholds, tables, and figures. Methods (imaging, stimuli, preprocessing/statistics) and participant demographics are described. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue fMRI task-evoked voxelwise results and related reporting. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol pictures) and a within-subject contrast of alcohol cues > neutral stimuli. Group-level voxelwise results are reported, including small-volume-corrected (SVC) ventral striatum findings (p<0.05 FWE for VOI) and MNI coordinates. Methods report participant age/sex (all male, ages provided), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts).

This is an fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual smoking images (meets I3). The analysis includes a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast (first-level GLM) used in higher-level analyses (meets I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using FSL Randomise within an anatomically defined mask (small-volume-corrected), with peak coordinates provided (meets I5 and I6). The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), satisfying I7. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The full text is an empirical fMRI study presenting visual cannabis, sexual, aversive, and neutral cues using a backward-masking paradigm. It reports within-subject voxelwise group-level contrasts (cannabis > neutral, sexual > neutral, aversive > neutral) with coordinates and cluster-corrected significance within an a priori ROI mask (small-volume correction) and provides methodological details (3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing, participant demographics). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue fMRI), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with small-volume-correction), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables), and I7 (participant/cue/MRI/preprocessing details). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines visual drug cues (cigarette images) and reports within-subject comparisons (cigarette vs pencil/chair) using MVPA in object-sensitive LOC (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the primary reported analyses are ROI-based MVPA confined to LOC voxels; the paper does not report any qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrast of drug cues>control stimuli (either whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) required by I5. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain/SVC result). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise cigarette>control contrast) and I6 is not applicable because there are no qualifying voxelwise results to be reported in tables/figures. Full text appears complete. Exclude on the basis of E3.

This fMRI study uses visual smoking cues (images of hands holding cigarettes vs neutral objects) and includes a within-participant contrast (smoking cue > neutral cue). Task-evoked voxelwise statistical results are reported: ROI-based small-volume-corrected (SVC) analyses on PCC/SCC with peak-level FWE-P < .05 (PCC) and exploratory whole-brain cluster-level FWE results. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), software (SPM12, CONN), and participant age/sex information. Thus it meets the review objective and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual methamphetamine cues in humans (non-treatment-seeking individuals with methamphetamine use disorder). It includes a within-subject drug-cue>control-cue contrast (Methamphetamine Cue>Control Cue) and reports whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results (Z-stat maps, cluster thresholds Z>2.3 and Z>1.96 with p<0.05) with coordinate tables and figures (supplementary tables/figures). Participant demographics (age, sex) and MRI details (3T Siemens Trio, preprocessing and FSL software) are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (ALC vs BEV blocks) and reports within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts, so it meets inclusion criteria I3 and I4. However, the imaging analysis is ROI-based: average BOLD timecourses were extracted from a priori 6-mm spheres and analyzed with hierarchical linear models. The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical maps/analyses (only ROI-average statistics are presented). Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine images (I3). The analysis includes within-participant contrasts of cocaine cues > neutral stimuli (COC > NEU) used in ROI analyses and regressions (I4). The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses using the COC > NEU contrast (FDR-corrected), i.e., group-level task-evoked voxelwise results are presented even though between-group differences were null (I5). Voxelwise results and activation maps are described and referenced in the main text/figures (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager, SPM/GLM details, FDR correction) are reported (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-participant contrast, non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not include a visual cue component (inclusion criterion I3 not met). The paradigm used individualized auditory guided imagery scripts (audio presentation and mental imagery), not visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts between favorite-food, stress, and neutral-relaxing conditions were performed), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported via whole-brain ICD analyses with FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures), and I7 (participant and methods details reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Because I3 is required for the meta-analysis objective (visual cue-reactivity), the study must be excluded despite meeting other criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual smoking cues (and matched control images) in a within-subject, placebo-controlled design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (smoking>control) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain repeated-measures ANOVA) with FDR-corrected results in ventral striatum and additional voxelwise results (p<0.001 uncorrected) reported in tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM2). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (tobacco, money, neutral) in daily smokers and reports within-participant contrasts (tobacco>neutral and money>neutral). The paper includes group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (voxelwise one-sample t-tests with cluster-level FWER correction via AlphaSim) and reports identified clusters/ROIs (coordinates referenced in supplement). Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual image stimuli (smoking vs neutral and smoking vs baseline). It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking>neutral and smoking>baseline) and group-level voxelwise statistical mapping with whole-brain correction (P<0.01 corrected), with coordinates and figures provided. Scanner field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager QX) and task/cue details are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for task-evoked, voxelwise visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is a resting-state seed/ROI connectivity study comparing smokers and non-smokers and does not include any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm or within-participant cue>control contrasts, nor does it report voxelwise task-evoked group-level results. Exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only with no qualifying voxelwise task result), E4 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity only without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result), and E5 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast) apply. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software) is satisfied. Inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study of drug/natural reward cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (at least one qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result), and I6 (availability of voxelwise cue-reactivity results in text/tables/figures) are not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > control (beverage) cues within the AUD group and reports group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with cluster-level corrected statistics (P < 0.05) and Talairach coordinates in tables/figures. MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99), cue type (visual alcohol images), and participant sex/composition are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for visual cue fMRI voxelwise results and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using pictorial alcohol cues (visual stimuli) in adolescents with AUD. The experiment includes within-subject contrasts of alcoholic > nonalcohol pictures and reports group-level voxelwise statistical comparisons (independent-samples t tests, clusterwise correction with voxelwise and clusterwise P thresholds) with coordinates/tables/figures. AFNI preprocessing/statistics are described. Although MRI field strength is not explicitly stated, this is a preferred (not mandatory) item and does not preclude inclusion. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol picture stimuli with an explicit within-participant contrast (alcohol pictures > neutral pictures). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (AFNI 3dLME, cluster-corrected via 3dClustSim; per-voxel p<.001, corrected α=.05) with coordinates/Z-values and cluster extents, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Reported methods include participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using photographic visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > control cues (both separately in satiated and 24-hr abstinent conditions) and direct paired comparisons. Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (one-sample and paired t-tests) with whole-brain results presented (tables/figures; p≤0.001 uncorrected, cluster threshold) satisfying the requirement for a group-level task-evoked voxelwise result. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (4.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The fulltext includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) and a within-participant contrast of alcohol cues > control (nonalcohol beverage) cues. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM (cluster-based BOLD fMRI results reported, spatial normalization to Talairach, results shown in Table 2 and figures), meeting the requirement for whole-brain/group voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (MEDx, SPM99) are reported. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

Exclusion criterion met: E3 (study reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (multimodal audiovisual cue paradigm includes a visual cue component), I4 (within-participant contrast of cocaine cues > neutral control segments was computed), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing details are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical maps or coordinate tables are reported for a task-evoked voxelwise analysis), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results are available in tables/figures as group-level voxelwise coordinates). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failing I5 and meeting E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual image stimuli. The authors report a within-participant contrast (smoking > neutral images) and performed group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANCOVA) with whole-brain cluster correction; results are reported as cluster coordinates (Table 1) and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (photographs), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although this is an fMRI cue‐reactivity study of cannabis that includes clear visual cues (and reports participant demographics), the paper reports ROI/network-based dynamic functional connectivity (DCC) analyses and topological metrics rather than any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. The meta-analysis requires at least one qualifying within-participant voxelwise cue>control contrast (whole-brain or SVC). Because the study provides only connectivity/ROI analyses (no qualifying voxelwise task activation results), it meets exclusion criteria E3 and E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cues present), I7 (demographic and methodological details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant voxelwise cue>control contrast reported), I5/I6 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results available). Full text appears complete.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (smoking and food videos) making it relevant to drug and natural reward visual cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant contrasts (Smoking>Food, Smoking>Baseline, Food>Baseline). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables (Table 1, Tables 2–3), satisfying whole-brain/statistically corrected reporting. Results are available in text, figures, and tables. Participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual photographic smoking cues. It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking cues > neutral cues) at the first level and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (multiple linear regression correlating HAMD with smoking>neutral BOLD) with tables/figures of coordinates. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (p<0.005 uncorrected, cluster extent threshold) and supplementary tables are referenced. Methods report participant age/sex, 3.0T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol-related pictures (I3). The main within-participant contrast alcohol > neutral is reported and used in group analyses (I4). Group-level voxelwise results are reported using whole-brain analyses and small-volume FWE-corrected results in striatal regions (I5), with coordinate reporting and figures/tables referenced (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing (SPM5), and statistical software are described (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not rely solely on ROI-only analyses (E3), connectivity-only or resting-state analyses (E4), nor does it only report between-group contrasts without within-participant cue>control contrasts (E5). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening. Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The full text contains a visual smoking-cue paradigm (videos) and reports within-participant contrasts (smoking cue vs fixation baseline; alcohol cue vs baseline). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are described (voxel-wise one-sample t tests across subjects with FDR control and cluster-wise inference; whole-brain activation maps and clusters are reported and plotted). Methods report participant demographics, scanner (3T), and preprocessing (FSL). Although the alcohol cue was a taste stimulus, the study is multimodal and includes clear visual cue components, satisfying the meta-analysis focus on visual cue-reactivity. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening.

This fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity includes a clear visual cue component (visual labels presented during taste delivery), uses a within-participant Alcohol>Water contrast, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected Z-statistic maps and coordinate tables). Results are reported in figures/tables and participant/sample/MRI/preprocessing details are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of eligibility.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking pictures (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral cues (I4) with group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (thresholded at z>2.3, cluster p<0.05 corrected) and lists activations/coordinates in the text and supplementary tables (satisfies I5 and I6). Methods include preprocessing and software (FSL) and participant sex/characteristics are reported; MRI field strength is not explicitly stated but missing details alone do not preclude inclusion (I7 is considered non-exclusionary). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using a clear visual stimulus paradigm (120 food images vs matched object images). It includes within-participant contrasts (food > object) at the subject level and group-level voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME1) with whole-brain permutation-based cluster correction; results reported as clusters/regions. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and statistical software (FSL), participant age/sex, and cue details. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI experiment in smokers using visual stimuli (cigarette-related, pleasant, unpleasant, neutral pictures). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing cigarette vs. neutral pictures and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cigarette > neutral) with thresholding and cluster coordinates (Table 2). Coordinates and statistical maps are reported in the main text/tables. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original human fMRI data). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete = false. Overall, this paper satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-evoked, visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (picture-perception task) with a within-subject contrast of alcohol cues > control stimuli. Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain one-sample t-test, FWE-corrected) and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses in the ventral striatum (FWE-corrected). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Exclusion criterion met: E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses visual drinking cues/multimodal design including visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrast of drinking cues > neutral/control cues was performed), I7 (participant demographics and acquisition/preprocessing details are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result is reported). Full text appears complete, and the exclusion is based on analytic reporting (ROI-only) relative to the meta-analysis requirement for voxelwise results.

Although the task includes visual cues (words 'Alcohol'/'Water') and the paper reports whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results (taste: alcohol taste > water taste), the manuscript does not report a within-participant contrast of visual drug cue > control cue (i.e., a cue-reactivity visual cue>control analysis). The reported qualifying whole-brain results pertain to taste/outcome contrasts and prediction-error analyses, not explicit visual cue>control cue-reactivity contrasts required by I4. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 and is excluded from the review of visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol-associated pictures with a within-participant contrast (alcohol-associated vs control stimuli). Group-level voxelwise second-level analyses were performed using SPM99 with reported whole-brain results (p<0.001, cluster size ≥5) and regions/tables are provided. MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99), participant ages/sex, and cue type are reported. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical design; a qualifying within-participant task-evoked voxelwise result is present).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > non-alcohol) and repetition contrasts (second vs. first presentation). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain cluster correction (cluster threshold determined by Monte Carlo, clusters >8127 μl, whole-brain α=.05), and a small-volume (anatomic NAcc) analysis was also performed. Methods report participant ages, sex/demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not include a clear visual cue component (it uses individualized script-driven imagery for stress, drug/alcohol cue, and neutral-relaxing conditions), thus failing inclusion criterion I3. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts: drug-cue vs neutral condition reported), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with family-wise error correction), I6 (results reported in figures/tables/supplement), and I7 (participant demographics and methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports a within-subject fMRI alcohol taste-cue task that includes a visual component (visual labels during taste delivery), and it computes an alcohol versus water (cue>control) contrast within participants. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported with cluster-based correction (Z > 1.96, p < .05) and peak MNI coordinates in tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Therefore it meets I3 (multimodal including visual cues), I4 (within-participant alcohol>water contrast), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise corrected results), I6 (results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (required methodological details provided). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examined fMRI cue-reactivity to cigarette (drug) cues with a visual component and reported within-participant cigarette>neutral (tape) contrasts in ROI analyses, and provided participant demographics and MRI details. However, it did not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Analyses are limited to predefined ROI mean-activation ANOVAs and ROI-based effective connectivity (uSEM/GIMME) without accompanying qualifying voxelwise results. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result) and E4 (reports only effective/seed-based connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI drug cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast analyses), I7 (participant and acquisition details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC task-evoked result). Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study explicitly examines alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol, stress, neutral images) and includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol cues > neutral and stress > neutral). Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise with family-wise error correction (p<0.001, cluster p<0.05) and report peak MNI coordinates and cluster results in main text/figures (supplement referenced). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (BioImageSuite), and statistical methods (AFNI 3dClustSim) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is a resting-state seed-based fMRI connectivity study examining median/dorsal raphe–hippocampal connectivity in smokers vs. nonsmokers and pre/post smoking. It does not include any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm with visual drug- or natural-reward cues and contains no within-participant cue>control contrast. Per the review criteria, it therefore meets exclusion criteria E4 (reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (task-evoked group-level voxelwise result), and I6 (availability of qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results in text/tables/supplement) are not met. No inclusion criteria relevant to cue-reactivity (I3–I6) are satisfied. Full text appears complete. Consequently, exclude from the meta-analysis focused on fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies.

This fMRI study uses visual cue-reactivity (video-based heroin and neutral cues), includes within-participant contrasts (heroin-cue vs neutral within runs; A2 vs A1) and reports group-level voxelwise results (cluster-thresholded, Talairach coordinates, Table I; Monte Carlo/Alphasim correction). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing (AFNI), participant demographics, and cue details. Voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are presented in text, tables, and figures, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI pharmaco-study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages) with within-subject contrasts (alcohol cues > neutral cues) computed at the single-subject level and entered into group-level analyses. The paper reports voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume-corrected (SVC, FWE) statistics within a priori ROIs (coordinates and pFWE values are provided for OFC, amygdala, VTA, etc.), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise evidence. Participant details, MRI parameters and preprocessing/statistical approach are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (task-evoked voxelwise results are present; the study is empirical human fMRI). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective (visual cue reactivity to a natural reward: food) and satisfies all inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study using visual food photographs (I3); reports within-participant contrasts of food cues > control stimuli (e.g., fattening food > object, all food > object) (I4); presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using voxelwise modeling (FLAME) within predefined anatomical masks with correction for multiple comparisons applied per region-of-interest (i.e., small-volume-corrected) (I5); results are reported in the main text with regionwise corrected clusters (acceptable per I6); and participant and MRI/preprocessing details (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner, FSL preprocessing/statistics) are provided (I7). Full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the paper qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Excluded per E3: This fMRI study used visual smoking cues (I3) and reported within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts (I4), and provided participant demographics (I7). However, reported analyses rely on ROI-extracted beta weights (caudate/NAc) and regression on those ROI values; the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results required by I5. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (I3). It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts of smoking vs neutral cues for crave and resist conditions (I4). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster correction (Z>2.3, cluster p=0.05) and coordinates/tables for clusters are provided (I5,I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies of drug-related rewards.

This study is excluded because it does not assess drug- or natural reward–related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and does not include any within-participant cue>control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked fMRI results from an N-back working memory task) and I7 (reports participant age/sex and MRI details). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no assessment of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues) and I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control or natural-reward-cue>control contrast). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply exactly (the study is not only ROI-only, it includes voxelwise task results; it is not only resting-state/ connectivity-only; and it does not present only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it does not satisfy the primary scope of the meta-analysis and should be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues vs neutral pictures (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral/control across sessions (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported with coordinates, thresholding, and corrected statistics (e.g., p(Bonf)<0.0001, FWE-corrected DMN results, cluster-corrected whole-brain seed analyses), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (I5). Voxelwise results are presented with coordinates and figures (I6). Participant details, cue type, MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (TurboBrainVoyager, BrainVoyager, AFNI, FSL) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion: E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of a natural reward with a visual cue — a light CS predicting juice) and I4 (within-participant contrasts involving the cue event vs other event types were analyzed, e.g., CS vs UCS/NTDE). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 is not satisfied because the paper’s reported analyses and results focus on a priori ROI mean-value statistics rather than presenting at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical result (no voxelwise coordinates or SVC-corrected clusters are reported in the provided full text or supplementary descriptions). I6 cannot be applied because no voxelwise results are available in main text, tables, figures, or supplements as provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so exclusion is based on analytic reporting (E3) rather than incomplete reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual pictorial stimuli and within-subject contrasts. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > soft drink) and pre/post training contrasts, and presents group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (family-wise error corrected) in anatomically defined ROIs (amygdala, nucleus accumbens) with peak coordinates and statistics. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are not required for eligibility. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual backward-masked cues (cocaine, sexual, aversive, neutral). It includes within-subject contrasts (cocaine vs neutral) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected thresholds) with coordinates and figures. Methods report scanner (3T), preprocessing (SPM8), and participant demographics. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking and food videos (I3 met). It reports within-subject network betas (Smoke, Food, Smoke-Food) derived from ICA temporal sorting and presents results as network-level component betas rather than group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. The manuscript does not report any qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) required by I5. Therefore it fails to meet I5 and does not provide the required drug-cue>control or natural-reward>control voxelwise contrast for inclusion (I4 not met). Exclusion criterion E4 applies because the study reports only component/network-level (ICA/temporal-sorting) analyses without a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue fMRI), I6 (results availability/format acceptable), I7 (participant and methodological details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue reactivity using visual stimuli (2-min smoking videos vs matched neutral videos). It uses within-subject contrasts of smoking>neutral, reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain cluster-corrected statistical results with peak coordinates and tables, and presents task-evoked results in figures/tables. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text. Therefore it fulfills the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrast, and qualifying voxelwise task-evoked group results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug-related) cue reactivity using visual picture stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol minus beverage) and group-level second-level voxelwise SPM5 analyses with reported cluster results and MNI coordinates (whole-brain voxelwise results reported and tabulated/figured). MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), and cue type (visual beverage pictures) are described; demographics are reported in Table 1. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual video stimuli (craving- and aversion-inducing videos). Within-participant contrasts (CIC vs mosaic control; AIC vs mosaic control) were computed and group-level voxelwise random-effects GLM results are reported with cluster/FDR thresholds and regional coordinates. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager), and participant demographics are reported. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity that includes visual stimuli (pictures) and multimodal (odors + pictures). Subject-level contrasts included HFHS vs LFLS and HFHS vs NF (cue>control) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses tested these contrasts (e.g., HFHS>LFLS pre–post and HFHS>NF pre–post) with reported cluster-level results (p=0.001 uncorrected, k=8) and region findings. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM12, DARTEL) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of nalmefene effects on emotion processing using emotional face stimuli and a dot-probe task in AUD patients, not a drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity paradigm. Inclusion criteria I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward cues>control) are not met — the task contrasts faces>forms (emotional/social stimuli), not drug or reward cues. The study does meet I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results), I6 (results reported in main text/figures), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address reward-related cue-reactivity (I3,I4 not met).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual cue videos. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette-related cues to neutral control (crave-allow vs neutral; crave-resist vs neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical results (FLAME, cluster-corrected thresholds) with coordinate tables and figures. Methods include MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing and analysis software (FSL/FEAT), and demographic/treatment variables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening purposes. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study with a visual cue-based monetary reward task (words displayed on screen) that includes a within-participant contrast of reward versus non-reward (50¢>0¢). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise threshold and cluster correction) with coordinates and cluster results, meeting the requirement for a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue-based drug/natural reward cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant contrast of reward>control: 50¢>0¢), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures), and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine-cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast (cocaine cues > neutral cues) at first level and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-corrected), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. Visual cue stimuli, participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Although the paper also presents effective connectivity (IMaGES) analyses, it additionally provides qualifying voxelwise GLM results, so it is not excluded by connectivity-only criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis’s requirement for a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise visual cue result. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the primary reported results are ROI-based correlations between DRD2 methylation and alcohol>juice activation; the whole-brain analyses reported were exploratory and did not pass whole-brain error correction, so there is no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (the paper includes a within-participant Alcohol>Juice contrast) and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8) are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the cue-reactivity task used gustatory/taste cues delivered via gustometer rather than a clear visual cue component) and I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked result reported that is whole-brain corrected or small-volume-corrected). Therefore the paper is ineligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis focusing on visual cue-reactivity voxelwise fMRI results.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli (appetitive images) with a within-subject contrast of food>neutral (scrambled) images. The study reports group-level voxelwise analyses including ROI-based small-volume-corrected results within the striatum (AAL/WFU PickAtlas) with FDR correction (p<0.05), and also reports whole-sample task effects. Methods include MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5); participant demographics and cue type are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity (I3), within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results (I5), with results reported in the main text/figures/tables (I6). Participant/scan details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because the alcohol-cue manipulation used individualized guided imagery (audio/script-based) rather than a visual cue component required by the meta-analysis (I3 not met). The paper does include a within-participant alcohol-cue > neutral contrast (I4 met) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with FWE correction (I5 met). Reporting of voxelwise results in figures/tables is present (I6 met), and participant/cue/MRI details are reported (I7 met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to failure to meet I3 (visual cue requirement).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (photographs) and reports a within-subject contrast (‘favourite drinks > neutral’) at the individual level and group-level voxelwise results. The paper provides whole-brain results (P<0.001 uncorrected) and small-volume-corrected ROI results (P<0.05 FDR) with coordinates, reports MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM5), and includes demographic details. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. These facts satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I3–I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual tobacco advertisement stimuli to probe cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts of ‘tobacco—control advertisement’ at the first level and includes group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level SPM5 analyses) with FDR-corrected results and cluster reporting, presented in figures and supporting tables. Participant demographics (age, all-male), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are clearly reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrast, qualifying group-level voxelwise results, results presented in figures/tables, and reporting of key methodological details). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual video cues (cocaine, food, neutral) in 20 active cocaine users. It reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine>neutral; food>neutral and contrasts vs fixation) and group-level voxelwise SPM8 analyses with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction and coordinate tables/figures. MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) are reported. Hence it satisfies all inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked visual cue-reactivity analyses, and none of the exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical data). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study of marijuana cue-reactivity using visual cues in treatment-seeking, marijuana-dependent participants. The study reports within-subject contrasts of marijuana cues > non-marijuana control cues at the group level, with voxelwise statistical results reported as cluster-corrected results within an anatomically defined ROI mask (small-volume correction) and peak coordinates in tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, MATLAB) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral images). It includes a within-subject contrast (smoke > neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results thresholded at Z>2.3, corrected cluster p=0.05 (tables and figures provided). Although the paper also reports a seed-based PPI, it additionally reports whole-brain task effects (smoke>neutral), satisfying the requirement that qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results be present. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related pictorial cues (I3). The main within-subject contrast heroin-related > neutral is explicitly reported (I4). Imaging analyses are group-level voxelwise mixed-effects (FLAME) with whole-brain cluster correction (qualifying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results) (I5). Voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures (I6). Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group without within-subject cue>control contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking > non-smoking control videos, reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps and peak coordinates (Tables S1–S2) and applies multiple-comparison correction (p < 0.05 corrected). Methods report MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing and statistical software, participant age/sex, and cue type. These aspects satisfy the meta-analysis objective (visual drug cue reactivity) and all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study with within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral, stress>neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise, cluster-corrected group-level results; participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. However, the experimental cues were personalized auditory imagery scripts (audio/imagery), not visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I3 requires a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal including visual cues), which is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded from the visual cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues with a within-subject contrast (smoking cues > neutral stimuli) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise SPM99 random-effects analyses. Results are reported as statistical parametric maps and tables of coordinates (figures/tables), MRI field strength (1.5 T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise group analyses of visual drug cue-reactivity and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual cue-reactivity paradigm in patients with opioid use disorder, reporting within-subject contrasts of drug vs neutral cues and group-level voxelwise results. The paper reports ROI analyses and a whole-brain session × stimulus ANOVA with a significant cluster in ventral striatum/mOFC (MNI coordinates provided) at a corrected threshold, fulfilling the requirement for a group-level task-evoked voxelwise result. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. Participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is a task-based fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity with visual cues and within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, and reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/processing details. However, the reported group-level analyses are ROI-averaged statistics (parameter estimates from 5-mm a priori spheres) rather than voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual smoking cue reactivity), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise group-level result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study used a visual cue paired with a natural reward (juice) and reports voxelwise whole-brain and SVC task-evoked results, but it does not present a within-participant cue>control (e.g., cue>neutral or cue>baseline) contrast that qualifies as a standard cue-reactivity analysis. Specifically: inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue with natural reward), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain and SVC results reported), I6 (results available in main text/supplement), and I7 (reporting of participant age range, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion I4 is not met: there is no clear within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues>control stimuli reported (analyses focus on event types/temporal-difference errors: CS, UCS, PTDE, NTDE, rather than a cue>control cue-reactivity contrast). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (no accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete for screening (intro, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual drug/alcohol cues (I3) and reports within-participant drug/alcohol-versus-neutral contrast betas used in generalized PPI connectivity analyses (I4). It also reports participant characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) (I7). However, the paper reports only task-modulated seed-based connectivity (gPPI) results between the VMPFC and predefined ROIs and does not present any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) or coordinate tables for task-evoked contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (only seed/effective connectivity results without qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (required voxelwise task-evoked statistical result). Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on E4; included: I3, I4, I7; not met: I5.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study in daily smokers that used visually presented cues indicating reward type (picture representing a puff, money, or neutral) and measured task-evoked BOLD responses. The authors report within-participant contrasts for puff>neutral and money>neutral during anticipation, and group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVA) with region-of-interest voxelwise inference and corrected cluster thresholds within anatomically defined masks; exploratory whole-brain results are also described. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual (picture) cues (with a sip prime), reporting within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > beverage cues and alcohol > control. The study acquired whole-brain BOLD images and performed voxelwise analyses using SPM/MEDx, reporting thresholded group-level voxelwise results (cluster extent corrected p<0.05) with tables/figures and coordinate/activation maps and reporting participant demographics, cue type, field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contains qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses visual heroin-related cues and reports within-participant contrasts (heroin-related > neutral) at the group level, but the reported voxelwise results are confined to a priori ROI masks and thresholded uncorrected (p<0.05, cluster>20 voxels) rather than reported as whole-brain corrected or small-volume-corrected results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I6 (voxelwise results reported in figures/main text), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related word cues and matched neutral words, with within-participant contrasts (drug > neutral) reported. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and a small-volume correction for the mesencephalon are reported with stereotaxic coordinates and cluster statistics. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing, and SPM2 software are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; missing supplemental materials are acceptable. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual picture cues. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > control cues and conducts group-level voxelwise second-level analyses (SPM2 two-sample t tests) with results presented as coordinates and tables. Analyses were conducted using a restricted anatomical mask (small-volume search) and significant voxelwise activations are reported (P≤0.005, cluster threshold), with MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistics (SPM2), cue type, and participant demographics reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task-evoked voxelwise results). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity using visual cigarette cues (participants held and viewed their cigarette), meeting the review objective. It includes a within-participant cue contrast (cigarette vs neutral) with a reported main effect of cue and instruction×cue interaction. Group-level voxelwise mixed-model ANOVA results are reported (voxelwise thresholds and cluster criteria) and tabulated (Tables 2 and 3) with stereotaxic coordinates, satisfying requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (NIS, AFNI), so preferred reporting elements are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using alcohol-related visual cues in a go/no-go task and reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol cues to control stimuli (e.g., Alcohol_nogo > Non-alcohol_go, interaction and main-effect contrasts). Group-level voxelwise second-level analyses are reported with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of significant clusters. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL) and participant demographics are reported. Thus the study meets the review objective and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cocaine/paraphernalia). It reports within-participant contrasts of cocaine cues > neutral controls (cocaine minus neutral) and whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (cluster-level inference in SPM8) with reported significant clusters/coordinates. Methodological details required by I7 are provided (participant ages, sexes indicated as men and women, 3.0T scanner, preprocessing with SPM8, acquisition parameters). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue reactivity using visual cannabis vs neutral stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts (cannabis > neutral). The paper presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and voxelwise t tests) with cluster-level FWE correction (pFWE < .05) and reports coordinates and region-level results; seed/connectivity analyses are presented additionally but do not replace the task-evoked voxelwise results. Participant demographics, cue type (visual cannabis images), and methodological details are reported (with further acquisition/processing details referenced in supplement). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine-dependent participants viewing visual smoking vs. matched neutral images (visual cue component), using a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported with cluster correction (p<0.05, Z=2.3) and coordinates in tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity RCT using visual alcohol vs non-alcohol beverage images (meets I3) with a within-participant ALC>BEV contrast (meets I4). Participant/sample details, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software (FSL/FEAT) are reported (meets I7). However, the reported imaging results are based on extraction of percent signal change from anatomically defined ROIs (right and left ventral striatum) and subsequent ROI-based statistics; no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables are presented in the provided full text. Therefore the study reports only ROI analyses and lacks a qualifying voxelwise result, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result). Conclusion: EXCLUDED (E3).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (favorite alcoholic drink images vs water) during a Pavlovian-instrumental transfer task. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol-related versus control (water/neutral) stimuli and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with a small-volume-corrected (SVC) finding in the right ventral striatum (NAcc; pFWE−SVC = 0.01). The paper provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of smoking cue (drug) reactivity using clear visual stimuli (still images in Study 2 and audio-visual videos including visual content in Study 1). Both studies include within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > control (SC versus non-SC). Study 1 reports group-level voxelwise GLM results within an a priori ROI mask with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction (i.e., small-volume-corrected voxelwise results reported with coordinates and t-values), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Results and coordinates are reported in the main text and supplementary materials; participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM/FSL) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using audiovisual (multimodal including visual) cues. The study reports a within-subject contrast of smoking cues > nonsmoking cues and performed whole-brain group-level analyses with small-volume correction (SVC) in a priori ROIs; significant cluster coordinates and figures/tables are reported (Table 2, Figures 1–2). Methods include MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/ASL toolbox), and participant demographics (age/sex, BMI groups). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrast, group-level voxelwise results with SVC, coordinates/figures available, and required reporting details). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing craved vs. control stimuli (Look Craved > Look Not Craved; Look Craved > Look Neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster correction (AlphaSim) and coordinate tables. The paper also reports MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant age/sex, and cue types. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (heroin-related pictures vs neutral), with within-subject heroin-related>neutral contrasts and group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (random-effects two-sample t-tests) with multiple-comparison correction (AFNI Alphasim Monte Carlo), and reports results in tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (visual and auditory cues; visual component present). Within-subject contrasts comparing high- vs. low-calorie food cues (cue>control type contrast) are reported pre- and post-surgery. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM5 with cluster-extent correction (p<0.05 corrected) and results are reported in text/figures; details on participants (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual cocaine-word cues with a within-subject CW>NW contrast (meets I3 and I4). However, the study reports no significant group-level voxelwise activations corrected for multiple comparisons (no whole-brain FWE or small-volume-corrected results). Only uncorrected cluster results (used for DCM node selection) are described, and the primary positive findings are from effective connectivity (DCM). Because there is no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise group result (whole-brain or SVC), the study does not meet I5 and therefore falls under exclusion criterion E4 (reports effective connectivity findings without a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result). Full text appears complete.

This study reports resting-state fMRI (seed-based rsFC and ICA) and DTI structural analyses comparing abstinent vs satiated smokers and nonsmokers; it does not present any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural reward cues, nor any within-participant cue>control visual contrast. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria requiring visual cue-reactivity and a within-participant cue>control task-evoked voxelwise result. Full text is complete (contains intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI cannabis word Stroop using visual cannabis-related words (visual cue component) and includes within-participant contrasts of cannabis-related versus neutral words. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume corrections (peak voxel coordinates and pFWE values reported for ROIs such as insula, amygdala, ventral striatum), satisfying the requirement for small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results. The full text includes methods (3T MRI field strength, SPM8 preprocessing), participant demographics (male, 18–30), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual heroin-related vs neutral picture cues (meets review objective). It includes a within-participant contrast (heroin-related > neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM8) with cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo) and results described in the main text and supplementary material. Participant/sample and MRI details are provided (male subjects, MMT patients and healthy controls, 3T scanner, preprocessing/statistics described). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Thus the study satisfies the required inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked cue>control results and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (ISIS images) with a within-participant event-related design modeling smoking and neutral images. The authors created subject-level contrasts and performed group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) reported with voxelwise thresholds (p<0.0001, cluster threshold) and location tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Although the smoking>neutral contrast did not yield significant activation differences, the within-participant contrast and group-level voxelwise results were explicitly performed and reported, satisfying inclusion requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore the full text is complete.

This is an event-related task fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues (images) and neutral visual cues, meeting the review focus on visual cue-reactivity. The paper reports within-subject “Heroin–Neutral” contrasts and within-group activations (and between-group contrasts), with group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise random effects two-sample t-tests) reported at P<0.05 FDR-corrected and cluster threshold—i.e., qualifying whole-brain task-evoked results with coordinate reporting. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and includes within-participant contrasts (highly desirable > less desirable food images and food > non-food). Second-level group voxelwise analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected p-values (i.e., qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistics (SPM8), participant age/sex, and cue types. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a resting-state fMRI study of insula connectivity following 12 h abstinence, not a task-based cue-reactivity study using visual drug or natural reward cues. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses reported). No inclusion criteria applicable: it does not include a cue-reactivity task with visual stimuli (I3 not met), contains no within-participant cue>control task contrast (I4 not met), and does not report any task-evoked group-level voxelwise results required for I5/I6. Full text appears complete and contains methods and results. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis of task-evoked visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual beverage cues (alcohol and non-alcohol images) in AUD patients and controls. The authors computed within-subject contrasts of each stimulus versus a mosaic baseline (stimulus>control) and conducted group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (full-factorial ANOVA) with FWE-corrected results and peak coordinates reported. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing (SPM12, MATLAB), and participant demographics are reported. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (I3). It contains a within-subject contrast of alcohol > neutral stimuli at the group level (I4). Voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain uncorrected clusters) and ROI small-volume-corrected results (FWE SVC) are presented, satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise evidence (I5). Results are described in the text with reference to tables/figures reporting coordinates and statistical maps (I6).
