Key methodological details are provided (participant age, MRI 3T field strength, preprocessing and analysis with SPM5), satisfying I7 (sex not explicitly detailed but this alone does not exclude the study). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol beverage pictures and emotional faces). The paper includes within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol and emotion picture trials to congruent control trials (e.g., alcpic > con), reports whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with cluster-based multiple-comparison correction (3dClustSim), and provides tables/figures of activation loci. MRI field (3T), participant demographics, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (relevant metadata reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not meet the review’s cue-type and within-subject cue contrast requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the paper does not include a qualifying within-participant drug-cue>control (or natural reward>control) contrast: it uses personalized stress guided-imagery (auditory) rather than visual drug/natural-reward cues, and the authors did not present a within-subject drug-cue>control voxelwise contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (voxelwise results/tables/figures provided), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no clear visual cue component — scripted auditory guided imagery was used), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues>control stimuli as required). Full text appears complete and sufficient for assessment.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol-related pictures versus neutral IAPS pictures (visual cues). It includes a within-participant contrast CUEalc > IAPSneutral and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results analyzed with SPM/BPM. Results are reported with small-volume FWE corrections in a priori ROIs and with whole-brain FWE-corrected peaks and coordinate tables/figures (Figures and Tables with MNI coordinates and FWE p-values). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, BPM, ArtRepair) are reported. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study is an empirical human fMRI investigation of drug cue-reactivity using visual (video) cigarette cues. It reports within-participant Cigarette Cues > Neutral Cues contrasts and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected at Z>2.3, p<0.05) with coordinate tables and figures. The manuscript provides necessary methodological details (3T scanner field strength, FSL preprocessing/statistics, participant demographics) and includes ROI and exploratory whole-brain analyses. Thus it satisfies the review’s requirements for visual cue component (I3), within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), and reporting of whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise results (I5/I6). Reporting of participant/method details is present (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrast, and is original empirical data). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (videos of cocaine and food) and includes a within-participant contrast of cocaine > food cues. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported (whole-brain cluster-corrected maps with p-thresholds, cluster sizes, and supplemental tables/figures). Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, AFNI preprocessing/statistical software) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes the required within-subject cue>control contrast). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This is an empirical perfusion fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity using audiovisual (including visual) smoking cues, with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues vs non-smoking control) and group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses reported in SPM2. Results are reported as cluster-level/voxelwise statistics with MNI coordinates (tables/figures), and participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are described in the full text. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise cue>control analyses with visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage images and reports within-participant ALC>BEV contrasts, but the imaging results are reported as ROI (right ventral striatum 6-mm sphere) percent signal change and subsequent GLM tests on extracted values. The paper does not present a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical map or coordinates for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result in the provided full text. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (required group-level voxelwise result). Included criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise group-level task-evoked results reported). Full text appears complete.

This report is a single-case fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and presents within-participant cue>control contrasts and fMRI BOLD activations (meets I3 and I4). The authors indicate voxelwise activations and supplementary fMRI results (satisfies I6). However, the study is a N=1 case report and does not provide a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) required by I5, so it is not eligible for the planned coordinate-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Therefore EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I5 is not met.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual cannabis cues (I3). It includes a within-subject contrast of cannabis images > neutral/control images (I4). Results include ROI small-volume-corrected analyses (VTA, OFC, ACC, striatum, amygdala) and whole-brain cluster-corrected results reported in text, tables and figures, fulfilling the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked group-level results (I5, I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported (I7). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant marijuana cues > control contrast is reported), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain cluster-corrected results reported with tables/coordinates), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables/figures), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (requires a clear visual cue component); this study used a tactile cue-exposure paradigm (tactile presentations of a marijuana pipe vs pencil) with no visual-only or multimodal visual cue component described, so it does not satisfy I3. No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E6 not met). Therefore, despite satisfying several fMRI reporting requirements, the absence of a visual cue component means the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis and should be excluded.

This is an empirical task-fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs low-calorie; food vs nonfood). Group-level voxelwise analyses are described and significant whole-brain cluster results are reported (cluster-thresholding with P<0.001), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM12), and other acquisition/statistical details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual heroin-related images (I3). It reports a within-participant contrast of heroin-related > neutral stimuli (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are presented (GLM second-level random-effects analysis, FDR-corrected voxelwise results, list of activated regions and coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence (I5). Voxelwise results are reported in figures/tables and described in the text (I6). Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to connectivity/resting-state analyses (E4), and include a within-subject cue>control contrast rather than only between-group contrasts (E5). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of heroin cue reactivity using visual stimuli (24 heroin, 24 neutral pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (heroin versus neutral) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM8) with cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates, and voxel-wise correlations; MRI field strength (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and reporting of whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports ROI-based analyses and used ROI-extracted contrast values in regressions, but did not report any qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) significant activation for the cocaine>neutral contrast. Inclusion met: I3 (visual cue component — cocaine words presented visually) and I4 (within-participant contrast cocaine>neutral was computed). Inclusion not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise result reported as significant/usable for meta-analysis), I6 (no available qualifying voxelwise coordinates/peaks to include), I7 (reporting details partially present but not sufficient to rescue lack of qualifying voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures and an alcohol taste) in alcohol-dependent participants, satisfying the review objective. Within-subject contrasts (alcohol minus beverage and other contrasts) are reported and used in the analyses. Group-level voxelwise results are reported using SPM2 (tables/figures of activation maps) and a region-based small-volume approach for the ventral striatum (6 mm ROI) with group-level statistics; thus at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise or small-volume analysis is present. Results are reported in tables and figures, and key methodological details are provided (MRI field strength 1.5T, preprocessing/statistical software SPM2, cue types, participant demographics). The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and should be included.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using visual smoking cues (photographs) and control images, meeting the review objective. It includes a within-participant smoking cue > control cue contrast entered into group-level voxelwise random-effects multiple regression analyses (task-evoked results). Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (tables/figures; gray-matter mask; p≤0.005, cluster threshold) and coordinate tables/figures are provided. Methods report MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), cue type, and participant demographics/sex; full introduction, methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual drug words and includes within-participant drug vs. neutral contrasts and detailed voxelwise reporting (coordinates) and methodological details. However, the key qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast (drug>neutral) does not yield any whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level statistical results: the reported voxelwise drug>neutral difference did not reach cluster-level corrected significance, and the significant drug>neutral effects relied on ROI/pairwise tests. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one group-level voxelwise task-evoked, whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result for the cue>control contrast. Exclusion ID E3 applies (only ROI results for the critical contrast). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI with visual cues), I4 (within-participant drug vs. neutral contrast performed), I6 (voxelwise results reported as coordinates/figures), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise cue>control result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using a visual cue-reactivity task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of cannabis vs. non-cannabis images (contrast maps created and carried to group-level tests), and conducted group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster correction (z>3.1, p=0.05). ROI (small-volume) analyses were also performed. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (visual cannabis cues), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for visual drug cue fMRI studies with qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Inclusion criteria applied: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug-related) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). The analysis includes a within-participant contrast of alcohol vs neutral cues (drug cue>control) (I4). Group-level voxelwise, whole-brain statistical results are reported (thresholds, cluster size, and significant posterior cingulate clusters) meeting the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (I5); results are presented in figures and described in the text (I6). Core methods (stimuli, MRI field strength 1.5T, AFNI preprocessing/statistics) and participant/sample information are provided; the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation presenting visual smoking-related pictures and neutral pictures, with within-participant contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) reported. It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: whole-brain cluster-corrected activation for smokers (ACC/OFC, SFG, occipital/fusiform) for the SR vs N contrast, and ROI voxelwise results in ventral striatum (reported with coordinates). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT, FILM, FLAME) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. Note: although VS/NAc ROI results were reported with uncorrected thresholds, the presence of other whole-brain corrected group-level voxelwise results satisfies I5.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual (and tactile) cannabis, natural reward (fruit), and neutral cues in long-term daily cannabis users and non-users. It includes within-participant contrasts (cannabis>neutral, cannabis>fruit, fruit>neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FEAT/FLAME) with cluster-level FWE correction and cluster-defining thresholds; results are described with cluster peaks and figures/tables (supporting information). MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, FSL/FEAT) and cue types are reported. Participant demographics (N, but ages/sex distribution not shown in provided excerpt) are partially reported; missing age/sex alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, within-participant contrasts present). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for voxelwise task-evoked cue-reactivity with visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug (cocaine) cue-reactivity in regular users with a described cue-reactivity task during fMRI, within-subject analyses of cue responses, and reported exploratory whole-brain analyses (with comprehensive results referenced in supplementary materials). The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, MRI acquisition at 3.0T, tasks), results, and discussion. Although the cue modality is not explicitly spelled out in the main text, cue-reactivity paradigms typically use visual cues and the manuscript states the cue-reactivity task was adopted from prior work; voxelwise whole-brain results are reported/exploratory and available in supplements (satisfying whole-brain/SVC reporting criteria). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol vs soft-drink cues (visual stimuli). It includes a within-subject contrast (alcohol blocks > soft drink blocks). The authors report group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (exploratory whole-brain results with reported peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected p-values) in addition to ROI analyses, satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, SPM8 preprocessing) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with clearly defined visual cues (geometric figures) predicting monetary gain/loss/neutral outcomes, meeting the review’s focus on visual natural-reward cue reactivity. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (gain > neutral; loss > neutral) at the group level and provides voxelwise statistical results (including coordinates) and small-volume-corrected (SVC, FWE-corrected) findings in the ventral striatum. Methods report participant demographics (male, age-matched groups), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), satisfying reporting preferences. The supplied full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion (E3) applies: the manuscript reports only ROI-based analyses (predefined 6-mm spherical ROIs with extracted BOLD timecourses entered into HLM/GLM) and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual image cues), I4 (within-participant contrast ALC>BEV was computed), I7 (participant age range, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, HLM, SPSS) are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and group-level voxelwise analyses reported as coordinates and statistical maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral and whole-brain random-effects fMRI results with peak coordinates), and discussion, so core content is present. Reported details include participant demographics (male smokers), cue type (smoking-related visual cues), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-based task-evoked voxelwise results.

This fMRI study examines natural reward-related cue-reactivity to visual food images, includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food images versus non-food control images, and reports group-level voxelwise results using ROI-based small-volume analyses (with coordinates and T-values) as well as exploratory whole-brain results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that includes visual cues (alcohol-related pictures), reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs control pictures/odors), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster-wise FWE correction (p<0.05). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT), and participant age/sex. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues (sublingual buprenorphine phMRI) with within-participant heroin-related vs. neutral contrasts. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (paired t-tests, thresholding and cluster extent, coordinates reported), and ROI follow-ups are secondary. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: there is no visual cue component — cue-reactivity was elicited using olfactory (ethanol odor) stimuli only. The study does meet I4 (within-participant ethanol odor > neutral air contrasts reported), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked SPM results / whole-brain maps reported), I6 (results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of functional connectivity in smokers, not a task-based cue-reactivity study using visual drug or natural reward cues. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrast is reported). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity task with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5/I6 (no task-evoked group-level voxelwise or small-volume-corrected results to report). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis eligibility and is excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related pictures. It reports within-participant contrasts (smoke vs rest; smoke and neutral conditions modeled) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (whole-brain thresholded maps reported, p≤0.005 uncorrected with cluster threshold), satisfying the requirement for a group-level task-evoked voxelwise result. Methods report participant demographics, cue type (visual smoking images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (TBV and SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in cocaine-dependent patients using visual stimuli (cocaine-related pictures). It includes within-subject contrasts of Cocaine>Neutral computed per participant and second-level group analyses. Voxelwise group-level results are reported, including small-volume FWE-corrected ROI analyses (e.g., VTA, ACC) and coordinates/t-values in the text/tables, and exploratory whole-brain results. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing and SPM8 software, and participant demographics. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses visual monetary cues (reward vs neutral) in a MID task, providing within-participant contrasts of reward>neutral for anticipation and outcome. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction in the bilateral nucleus accumbens (peak z, MNI coordinates, corrected p-values), satisfying voxelwise SVC reporting. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (monetary visual cues), 3T MRI scanner, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), meeting reporting expectations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject ALC>BEV contrast. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-level FWE correction (p<.05) and provides peak coordinates and tables/figures. Participant/sample, MRI parameters, preprocessing, and statistical software are described in the methods. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue paradigms and qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cannabis-related cues in schizophrenia patients with comorbid cannabis use disorder. It includes within-subject contrasts (cannabis vs. neutral images) and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE-corrected statistics and peak coordinates (e.g., amygdala, thalamus, insula; pFWE values given). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing software (SPM8), participant demographics (male, age 18–30), and cue type are reported. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the fMRI cue-reactivity task used olfactory (odor) cues during imaging with eyes closed and no pictures presented during the scans. Although participants underwent a pre-imaging familiarization with combined odor+picture exposure, the actual fMRI measurements were driven by odor-only stimuli, so the study lacks a clear visual cue component during imaging. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant AO>ApCO contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise SPM results / reported peaks), I6 (results reported in figures/coordinates), and I7 (participant and methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is not eligible for a meta-analysis restricted to studies that include a visual cue component in the fMRI task.

This study reports resting-state fMRI functional connectivity and mediation analyses relating trait alexithymia to tobacco craving; it does not include any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural reward cues, nor any within-participant cue>control contrasts. Therefore it lacks task-evoked, voxelwise group-level results required for inclusion. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity only without qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criterion met: I7 (reporting of participant age/sex and methodological details). Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5 (no visual cue-reactivity task or cue>control voxelwise analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete and reports a task-evoked, group-level, voxelwise alcohol>control contrast with cluster-corrected whole-brain results (satisfies I4 and I5). Results are reported in tables/figures and preprocessing/statistical software are described (I6, I7). However, the cue modality is gustatory (taste cues: alcohol vs. litchi juice), not visual; the meta-analysis requires a clear visual cue component (I3). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (visual cue requirement) despite meeting I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual cues (game screenshots and smoking images) to elicit cue-reactivity. Within-participant contrasts of gaming cues > neutral and smoking cues > neutral are reported. Group-level voxelwise results are presented (p<0.05 FDR corrected; and group effects with small-volume correction), with coordinates and ROI/SVC results described. MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), and participant demographics (age range, all male, right-handed, n=16 per group) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study of drug-cue reactivity using visual stimuli (cocaine-related words) and includes a within-participant cocaine>neutral contrast. The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected) and small-volume-corrected analyses (IFG mask), with clusters and contrasts described in the text. Imaging parameters (3T scanner), preprocessing/statistical software (CamBA; SPM referenced), participant demographics, and cue type are reported. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related pictures. It includes a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > neutral cues and reports group-level voxelwise results (cluster-corrected whole-brain group analysis with MNI coordinates and corrected p-value). Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, MATLAB), and participant demographics (age, sex). Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts (food > non-food, high-calorie > non-food, high > low) and reports group-level whole-brain corrected voxelwise results (Z>2.3, p<0.05, whole-brain corrected) with coordinates. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), participant age/sex, and cue types are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-participant contrasts).

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual cue pictures (water-related and drug-related) in heroin users, with within-participant contrasts (Thirst vs Neutral; Drug vs Neutral). Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise SPM2 statistics with reported voxelwise thresholds and Talairach coordinates (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (pictures of alcoholic beverages, food, and items) and tests within-subject contrasts of alcohol versus control stimuli (e.g., (2×ALC_high) – (FOOD_high + ITEM_high) and related high-risk vs low-risk contrasts). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results reported with cluster correction (z>2.3, cluster p<0.05) using FSL, and figures/tables/supplementary material present statistical maps/coordinates. Participants, scanner (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity in drug/natural rewards and is included.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts including alcohol-cue viewing versus baseline (reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates/tables) and condition contrasts (prayer > passive/news) that modulate cue responses. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, NeuroElf), and participant characteristics are described. Results include whole-brain corrected voxelwise findings (tables/figures) meeting eligibility. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study of visual smoking cues meets I3 (drug cue fMRI with visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant smoking>control contrasts via repeated-measures analyses), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, 1.5T field strength, and preprocessing/statistics: SPM99/MATLAB). However, the paper reports only ROI-based analyses (manual ROIs with mean percent-signal ANOVAs) and explicitly notes the exclusive use of ROI methods; no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (coordinate tables or voxelwise SVC/WB results) are reported. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Excluded on grounds of E3; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7; inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI BOLD responses to standardized visual affective stimuli and to pictures of alcoholic versus neutral beverages in alcohol-dependent participants. The methods and results describe within-participant contrasts to affective and alcohol-related images and group-level voxelwise activation differences (e.g., reduced insula activation and other clusters; referenced table S3 with coordinates), indicating whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results are available. Participant and cue details are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity fMRI, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise reporting. Full text appears complete (supplementary tables are referenced but their absence does not preclude inclusion).

This is an fMRI study of visual drug cues that reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for contrasts of non-studied (new) versus studied (repeated) drug cues (priming). However, it does NOT present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (or natural reward cues > control stimuli), which is required (I4 not met). Included: I3 (visual drug cue fMRI), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results), I6 (results reported in tables/figures). Not met: I4 (no drug-cue > control contrast; only new vs. repeated cue contrasts), I7 (study reports sex, cue type, and preprocessing software but does not report participant ages or MRI field strength). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (32 ISIS images) and matched neutral cues during a task. It reports a within-participant contrast of smoking cues versus neutral cues (SCs − NCs) at the group level using SPM2 second-level voxelwise analyses (one-way ANOVA and t-contrasts) and provides voxelwise results with cluster sizes, t-values and coordinates (e.g. right insula at [46,4,0]). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Although thresholding was uncorrected and analyses were performed within an a priori mask, the paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results suitable for coordinate-based synthesis. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual images (food vs. non-food). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food, and the methods/state that group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses of food vs. non-food were conducted and are available in the Supplementary material. Participant age/sex (young adult females), cue type (food images), MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. The main ROI results do not preclude inclusion because qualifying voxelwise group-level results are indicated as available (Supplementary data), which satisfies the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results (I5) and allowance for reporting in supplementary materials (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical fMRI data present). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material is noted but its absence from the provided text is acceptable. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and violates none.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual picture stimuli (gambling and smoking pictures). It includes within-subject contrasts of gambling>neutral and smoking>neutral and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM2) with FWE correction and coordinate/figure reporting. MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), participant sex, and cue types are reported. The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures vs neutral houses), with within-participant alcohol>neutral contrasts. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (SPM8, voxel thresholds, AlphaSim cluster correction) with MNI coordinates and cluster sizes. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software, and participant demographics. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is original empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in nicotine-dependent smokers using visual smoking cues (images/videos) and a within-subject crossover design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues vs neutral cues and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (coordinates, t-values, and cluster sizes) from whole-brain analyses and ROI analyses. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T field strength, preprocessing with SPM8) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-cue videos and a mosaic control, reporting within-participant alcohol>control contrasts and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (GLM, RFX) with FDR cluster correction. The paper provides cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager BVQX), and participant demographics. Results are reported as voxelwise clusters/tables/figures. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual heroin-related stimuli (48 heroin-related images vs 48 neutral images), with an explicit within-participant contrast drug cue > neutral. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (voxelwise paired t-tests and whole-brain correlations) with cluster correction (z>=2.3, P<=0.05) and peak coordinates reported. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens Tim Trio 3T), preprocessing and analysis software (FSL, FEAT/FILM), and participant demographics (age/sex). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). It includes within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) at first level and reports group-level voxelwise analyses using masked (ROI) small-volume-corrected voxelwise inference (RANDOMISE with TFCE and FWE correction). Results are reported with cluster statistics and MNI coordinates. Key methodological details (participant age range, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing and statistical software: FSL/FEAT, ICA-AROMA, RANDOMISE) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not purely ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes qualifying within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food pictures. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>control pictures, presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain FDR-corrected maps (and uncorrected maps for interactions) and tables/figures with coordinates, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This fMRI study examines natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using visual predictive cues (images signaling chocolate milk vs tasteless solution) and actual receipt. It includes within-participant contrasts (anticipation: chocolate milk cue vs tasteless cue; consummation: chocolate milk receipt vs tasteless receipt). Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed with reporting of results using small-volume correction (FWE p<0.05) in a priori ROIs; results are reported in figures/tables. Key methodological details (participant demographics, cue type, 3.0T MRI, SPM8 preprocessing/statistics) are provided. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cigarette images (appetitive smoking images). It includes within-participant Craving>Neutral contrasts and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain cluster-corrected analyses with coordinates, t-values, and cluster sizes using Monte Carlo simulation). Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing and analysis software, and participant demographics. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-participant contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking images) and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking>neutral images. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (random-/mixed-effects GLM) with cluster correction (p<0.05), and results (regional activations) are reported. The paper provides participant characteristics (sex, age), MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager), and coordinate-based results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses visual cocaine-related videos (meets I3) and reports participant details and MRI parameters (meets I7). However, it does not report a within-participant task-evoked cue>control voxelwise contrast (no drug-cues>control contrast reported) nor a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result suitable for a cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Instead, the paper reports seed-based functional connectivity and wavelet transform coherence (WTC) analyses (time–frequency/ROI-based connectivity), which are connectivity-focused rather than task-evoked voxelwise contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity/resting-state/seed-based analyses only without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 and I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 and I7. Full text appears complete.

This study employed visual smoking cues and a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast (I3, I4). It performed whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported uncorrected cue>neutral activations (figure described), and provided methodological details (3T scanner, BrainVoyager, male participants), satisfying I6 and I7. However, the critical cue-reactivity contrast did not yield any results that survived correction for multiple comparisons, and no whole-brain FDR-corrected or small-volume-corrected significant voxelwise task-evoked results are reported for the smoking>neutral contrast; therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met beyond this failure to satisfy I5. Consequently the study is excluded because it lacks a qualifying corrected voxelwise cue-reactivity result (I5 not met) despite meeting I3, I4, I6 and I7.

Although this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking cues and reports within-subject smoke>rest percent signal change (PSC) contrasts, the reported analyses are ROI-based (participant-tailored ACC ROI and an IFG control ROI). The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (no coordinate tables or SVC/whole-brain contrast maps are provided in the main text). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual drug cue fMRI), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I7 (participant/scan/preprocessing details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise or SVC result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study directly addresses the review objective: it used visual heroin-related cues (48 pictures) in an event-related cue-reactivity fMRI task and modeled a within-subject drug>neutral contrast. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (regions significantly activated for heroin vs. neutral; P<0.001, uncorrected; peak PCC coordinate and cluster reported and shown in figures/tables). The paper therefore provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise task results rather than only ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported and the full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, lack of within-participant contrast, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol and soft-drink cues (visual stimuli) with both within-subject cue-related contrasts and group-level voxelwise results. The main analysis includes an interaction contrast comparing alcohol vs soft-drink approach/avoid conditions ((approach alcohol>avoid alcohol)>(approach soft drink>avoid soft drink)), which constitutes a within-participant alcohol vs control cue contrast. Results are reported as voxelwise coordinates with small-volume-corrected (SVC, FWE) statistics in a priori ROIs (NAcc, mPFC, amygdala), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report participant ages/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking and control videos (visual cues). It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking>control (averaged per 2-min blocks) and presents group-level voxelwise statistical maps with corrected inference: whole-brain cluster/peak correction and a predefined DLPFC small-volume correction (search region, SVC threshold reported). Coordinates and peak tables are provided in the main text/tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (fmristat) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for visual cue component (I3), within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), group-level voxelwise whole-brain and SVC-corrected results (I5), acceptability of coordinate/table reporting (I6), and reporting of needed methodological details (I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study uses a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with clear visual cues signaling reward/loss (satisfies I3). It reports within-subject contrasts of reward anticipation versus non-incentive and gain versus non-gain outcomes (satisfies I4). Group-level voxelwise statistical maps are presented and reported with familywise correction (Monte Carlo simulation) and voxelwise t-tests (satisfies I5 and I6). Methods report participant ages/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software (AFNI) (satisfies I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural (monetary) rewards with visual cues.

Although this is an fMRI study of visual drug-related cues with within-subject contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) and reports participant demographics and scanning parameters, the analysis is based on predefined region-of-interest (ROI) percent-signal-change measures rather than group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps. Inclusion criterion I5 (at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise or small-volume-corrected result) is not met. This triggers exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses without qualifying voxelwise results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I7). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion E3 met: the fMRI results reported in the paper are presented as ROI-extracted percent signal change and between-group ANOVAs rather than as group-level voxelwise, whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical maps. Although the methods state that whole-brain tests were performed, the results report ROI-based effects (OFC, ventral striatum) and extracted-signal comparisons; no qualifying voxelwise, whole-brain or SVC-corrected task-evoked voxelwise statistics or cluster coordinates are clearly reported for the fMRI drug>control contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity with visual cues — drug words were used as visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrasts: drug>fixation and drug>neutral reported), I6 (voxelwise results may be reported in figures/tables — the paper includes a figure with MNI coordinates), and I7 (participant sex, cue type, field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result is presented). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study using visual cannabis cues (images) and reports group-level, whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise results (Z>2.3, p<.05). The main neuroimaging contrasts are within-participant (approach vs avoid blocks that incorporate cannabis vs control images) and the paper also analyzed individual condition>baseline contrasts; voxelwise activation maps and clusters are reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME) are reported. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for visual drug-cue reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant task contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes visual stimuli (multimodal visual+auditory). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food cues>control (high-ED vs low-ED, and food vs nonfood) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with coordinates and cluster thresholds (Table 1, figures, and supplemental materials). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (drug words presented visually) with within-subject contrasts (drug vs. neutral words). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-level correction and small-volume corrections for a priori ROIs, including tables/coordinates and figures. Methods report participant demographics (age, gender), cue type, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s key inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity visual fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical human fMRI data).

This is an fMRI study using visual picture cues (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, emotional) and reports within-participant contrasts of drug-related cues > neutral control. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (tables/figures/coordinates) using FSL; MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and statistical methods are described. Participant demographics and cue types are reported. Although the sample is small (N=10), this does not violate inclusion criteria. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in alcohol-dependent participants that uses a multimodal cue paradigm including visual presentation (written statements) plus gustatory alcohol vs isocaloric control (litchi) cues. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > control cues (separately following Change Talk and CounterChange Talk), and group-level voxelwise whole-brain mixed-effects analyses with cluster correction (FLAME, cluster p<.05, z>2.3), with coordinates/tables and figures. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for a multimodal design that includes visual cues, a within-participant cue>control contrast, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts of hedonic food cues > non-food control stimuli, and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected via AlphaSim) with MNI coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant demographics, and cue type. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an fMRI task-based study that used visual cue stimuli (images indicating monetary reward, cigarette puffs, or neutral) and performed within-subject contrasts (money > neutral; puff > neutral) at the group level. The manuscript reports voxelwise group-level results from a random-effects ANOVA, identifying significant clusters in a priori striatal ROIs (voxel counts and coordinates reported) consistent with small-volume/ROI-corrected voxelwise statistics. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T Siemens Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore it meets criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (picture blocks) and a validated visual cue-reactivity task. The analysis includes an explicit within-participant contrast of alcohol > neutral (“alcohol - neutral”) and reports group-level voxelwise results from whole-brain analyses (cluster-level FWE correction determined via Monte Carlo/AlphaSim). MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5/SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity using visual smoking vs neutral pictures (visual cues). It reports a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-wise correction (3dClustSim), with activation maps and statistical results described in the main text. Participant/sample characteristics (male adult smokers), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This task-based fMRI study investigates visual cue-reactivity to drug, erotic, aversive, and neutral images (meets I3) and computes within-participant contrasts (drug-related > neutral) using ICA-derived component time-course GLMs (meets I4). However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (neither whole-brain nor small-volume-corrected voxelwise contrasts or coordinate tables of task activation). Instead, the main inferential results are network/component-level (ICA spatial maps and GLM on component time courses). Because no qualifying voxelwise task-evoked statistical result is provided, inclusion criterion I5 is not met. This violation places the study into exclusion category E4: studies reporting only ICA/other network analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result. Therefore the article must be excluded from the voxelwise meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward cues) vs neutral images (AC>NC) with within-subject contrasts and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. The full text contains introduction, methods (3T MRI, task, preprocessing and whole-brain GLM), results reporting voxelwise clusters and statistics, and discussion, so it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity. No exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion met: E3 — the study reports ROI/structure-averaged analyses (percent signal change over anatomical masks) and presents uncorrected masked F-maps; no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results are reported. (b) Inclusion met: I4 — within-participant contrasts comparing nicotine-anticipation vs saline (control) are present; I7 — participant age/sex and methodological details are reported. (c) Inclusion NOT met: I3 — no clear visual drug cue component (anticipatory cues were verbal/auditory; visual slides shown were neutral IAPS images for boredom reduction, not drug cues); I5 — no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked statistical result is provided; I6 — not applicable because qualifying voxelwise results are not available in tables/figures. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Thus the study does not meet all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and is excluded.

This fMRI study used visual reward cues (rings of dollar signs vs neutral pound signs) in a task designed to assess reward-related cue effects on antisaccade performance. It includes within-participant contrasts of Reward versus Neutral (reward>control) and reports group-level mixed-effects fMRI analyses. Although primary results are ROI-based, the authors generated z-statistic images for the predefined ROIs and applied voxelwise false-discovery-rate correction within those ROIs (i.e., small-volume correction), satisfying the requirement for a task-evoked voxelwise (small-volume-corrected) result. Information on participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) is reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral/control cues (e.g., “contrast ‘alcohol-neutral stimuli’”) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses with tables/figures and reported coordinates). The paradigm clearly involves alcohol-related cues and produced visual-system activations, consistent with a visual cue component. Results are reported as voxelwise statistical maps/tables (whole-brain, p-values, cluster sizes) and figures; supplementary materials are referenced. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment of criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion requirements for fMRI cue-reactivity studies using visual drug-related cues.

The study is excluded because it does not report the required within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (I4 not met). It used visual alcohol cues (I3 met) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (e.g., win>lose contrast with coordinates and FDR correction) meeting I5, reports results in figures/tables (I6), and provides participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (I7). However, no voxelwise alcohol-cue > neutral/control contrast (with whole-brain or small-volume corrected coordinates) is presented in the main text, tables, or figures, so the primary inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list directly apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards). It reports within-subject contrasts of food > control (scrambled) pictures, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain thresholding and small-volume (ROI/FWE) correction, and coordinates/tables. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (appetizing, bland, disgusting, non-food), satisfying the review objective. The study includes within-participant contrasts of appetizing>non-foods and appetizing>bland foods, and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: small-volume-corrected ROI results in dorsal and ventral striatum (FWE svc) and whole-brain uncorrected analyses. Necessary methodological details are reported (3T scanner, SPM5 preprocessing, cue types, participant groups and hunger ratings). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; reports task-evoked voxelwise results; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts; is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion)."

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (visual food cues) reporting within-participant food>nonfood contrasts and group-level voxelwise results (figures and coordinates). The paper reports MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, SAS/SPSS), participant age/sex, and other relevant details. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual natural reward cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrast, and qualifying group-level voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues predicting cigarette (drug) and monetary (nondrug) reward, with an event-related design and behavioral measures of cue-elicited motivation. It includes within-participant contrasts of reward-predicting cues (parametric anticipation contrasts across reward levels, effectively reward>control/baseline) for both cigarette and monetary cues. Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed (SPM5) with whole-brain inference (FWE correction applied; results reported with coordinates and t-values). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), cue type (visual), and participant information are reported or referenced. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s fMRI cue-reactivity inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using dynamic visual stimuli (movie clips). It includes a within-participant contrast of smoking scenes > matched nonsmoking control scenes, and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise results (thresholded maps and coordinate table). Methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant demographics, and cue type. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The task included high-calorie, low-calorie, and non-food (control) picture regressors and reporting of task-evoked, group-level voxelwise contrasts (whole-brain, FWE-corrected) with MNI coordinates in figures/tables. The analysis pipeline describes within-subject GLM regressors for food and non-food stimuli (allowing food>control contrasts), and results present voxelwise condition and condition×task effects and whole-brain correlations with plasma measures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only without within-subject cue>control contrast, or non-empirical) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is present and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette smokers using visual smoking videos (and neutral control videos) with a within-subject design. The authors report smoking>neutral (cue-reactivity) contrasts after stress and non-stress conditions, present group-level voxelwise activation maps, correct for multiple comparisons (p<0.05 corrected) and report peak coordinates and region-level ROI analyses. Participant demographics (age range, sex distribution), cue type (video smoking vs neutral), MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (fmristat) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual food cues (palatable food pictures) and matched scrambled control images in a within-participant design. It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (food>control) and uses small-volume FWE correction within a priori ROIs, yielding a significant right amygdala result (pFWE = .006). Imaging methods, preprocessing, MRI field strength (3T), and software (SPM5) are reported. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity, a within-subject cue>control contrast, and at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected result. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts (HC vs LC food cues) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results (second-level repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster-level FWE correction. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), participant demographics (age/sex), and cue types. Results (DLPFC activation, PPI connectivity) are reported in the main text with references to supplementary tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is an empirical human fMRI study).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (photographs of alcohol, non-alcoholic beverages, positive and negative emotional pictures). The analyses include within-participant contrasts (alcohol > non-alcoholic beverage; negative > beverage; positive > beverage) and group-level voxelwise statistics (one-sample t-tests and 2×3 ANOVA), with cluster results reported and coordinates/tables referenced; additional family-wise-error corrected results are reported for some comparisons. MRI field strength (1.5 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are specified. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual images (I3). It includes a within-participant contrast of alcohol>neutral (I4). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: whole-brain analyses and anatomically defined ROI analyses with FWE small-volume correction in the bilateral amygdala; coordinates and statistical values are provided (I5, I6). Methods report participant demographics, 3T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM) (I7). The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrast).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue conditioning using novel visual stimuli (geometric CS) with within-subject contrasts between CS+ (alcohol-paired) and CS− (saline-paired). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed (SPM5), with whole-brain cluster-corrected results reported and coordinates provided. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; includes within-participant cue contrasts; is original empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a natural reward (chocolate) that includes clear visual cue components (pictures of chocolate) and multimodal conditions. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., chocolate in mouth vs. tasteless rinse and picture of chocolate vs. grey control), group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with whole-brain and small-volume-corrected results (peaks reported), and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical details. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study includes fMRI with visual alcohol cues (I3) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results for emotional face contrasts (I5), with results shown in figures (I6) and demographic/MRI details reported (I7). However, the paper does not report a qualifying within-participant drug-cue (alcohol) > control (neutral) group-level voxelwise contrast: alcohol-picture results are stated as “no effect” and ‘data not shown,’ so no usable alcohol cue>control voxelwise maps or coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because there is no accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast for drug cues despite between-group testing. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol vs neutral/abstract) and conducts group-level voxelwise analyses in SPM5 with reported coordinates and cluster sizes, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistics are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; includes within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-associated pictures and IAPS affective (positive/negative/neutral) images, with within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral; positive>neutral; negative>neutral). Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (2-sample and 1-sample t-tests) with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates presented in tables/figures, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies and should be INCLUDED.
