The study is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual smoking-related images (both aversive and appetitive) presented to chronic smokers. It reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (aversive smoking-related vs neutral; appetitive smoking-related vs neutral). Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed (one-sample t-tests) with whole-brain exploratory analysis and cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo/3dClustSim), and results are presented in the main text and supplementary materials. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant contrasts, empirical task-based fMRI). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore this study meets the inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in nicotine-dependent participants using visual smoking and matched neutral images, reporting within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts. A group-level whole-brain mixed-effects (FLAME) voxelwise analysis (cluster-corrected p<0.05, Z>2.3) is reported, and results are further interrogated via ROI extractions. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (FSL) and other methodological details are provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses a monetary incentive delay task (MIDT) that employs visual cues signaling potential monetary rewards (natural reward-related visual cues). It reports within-participant contrasts of gain versus nongain (i.e., reward cue > control) and examines these contrasts at the group level. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected) and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (SVC in SPM2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI methods, and analysis software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI meta-analysis of drug/natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for a visual cue component (I3). The cue-reactivity task used gustatory (taste) alcohol cues delivered via a gustometer (alcohol vs lychee juice) and did not present alcohol-related visual stimuli or a multimodal design that clearly includes visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast alcohol>control present), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain results reported and corrected), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/supplement), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength [3T], and preprocessing/statistical software). Exclusion criteria: none applicable (E3–E6 not met). Full text appears complete and provides methods, results, and discussion. Therefore excluded based on failure to satisfy I3 (no visual cue).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures). The task used visual-only alcohol vs neutral blocks and computed within-subject contrast 'alcohol—neutral' per participant. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster thresholds, tables and figures reporting peak coordinates and significant clusters). Participant demographics (N=86, sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5/SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7).

This is a behavioral cue-reactivity study using personalized videotaped and in vivo alcohol cues; it does not report any functional MRI data or MRI methods, and no voxelwise task-evoked group-level results are presented. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of the listed exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: none — although the study uses visual cues, it is not an fMRI study. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study), I4 (no within-participant fMRI cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported), and I7 (MRI details not reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) but contains no fMRI analyses. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet core fMRI-specific inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images. The report includes within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected Z=2.3, p<0.05) with tables/coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical human neuroimaging study of drug-cue reactivity using visual cues and within-subject contrasts; however, it used PET (H2^15O) rather than functional MRI. The review’s inclusion criterion I3 requires functional MRI. Although the study provides within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts (drug video vs neutral video) and reports group-level voxelwise SPM results (satisfying I4, I5, I6), it fails I3 (fMRI modality). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not meet the modality-specific inclusion criterion (I3).

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports only ROI-based analyses (extracting average beta values from a priori 4mm spheres and using these in Cox/logistic regressions) with no group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked statistical results presented. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual smoking images), I4 (within-participant contrast of smoking cues > neutral/control stimuli), and I7 (reports participant demographics and methodological details). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level result was reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related images and neutral images. It includes within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral) with subject-level beta maps and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction. Voxelwise results (regions, statistics, cluster-corrected thresholds) are reported in the main text and connectivity results are supplementary but do not replace the task-evoked contrasts. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager, GIFT), cue type (visual images), and participant sex. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using audiovisual (multimodal including visual) smoking cues and a non-smoking control video, with within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking cues. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (cluster-wise corrected whole-brain analyses showing mOFC and other clusters) using SPM8, and methodological details (participant age/sex, 3.0T MRI, preprocessing/statistical approach) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue reactivity. It uses visual food images (high- vs low-caloric) meeting I3. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing high-caloric > low-caloric (separately in water and tea conditions) and interaction contrasts, meeting I4. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (exploratory whole-brain tests and ROI small-volume-corrected results; coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values reported), satisfying I5 and I6. Participant demographics, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported, meeting I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of nondrug (monetary) reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (shape cues and word cues). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing reward-predictive cues versus non-incentive cues (pre-response reward anticipation: $1/$10 vs $0), post-response WIN vs HIT cue contrasts, and reward notification contrasts (wins vs non-wins). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are reported (whole-brain analyses with FDR correction) and activation maxima are listed in tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, 3dMEMA) are reported. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine-deprived smokers using visual cigarette cues and within-participant contrasts, but the reported analyses are primarily ROI-based (a priori anatomically defined ROIs and comparisons of mean beta coefficients). The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain results or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical maps/coordinates needed for inclusion. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise (whole-brain or SVC) group-level task-evoked result.

The full text reports only ROI-based analyses (mean BOLD across anatomically defined ROIs with repeated-measures ANOVAs) and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (no coordinate tables, voxelwise maps, or SVC results are reported). This violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). The study does meet I3 (fMRI study with visual smoking cues), I4 (within-participant smoking>control contrasts were analyzed), and I7 (participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details reported). It does not meet I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result) and I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical BOLD-fMRI task study using visual natural reward (food) cues with within-subject food vs. non-food contrasts. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (exploratory whole-brain FDR cluster-corrected analysis showing OFC and VS) and also provides ROI and coordinate-based results. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner details, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts of interest (e.g., Look Craved > Look Neutral; Look Craved > Look Not Craved). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with cluster-correction (AlphaSim) and coordinates for significant clusters; the paper also interrogates the small ventral striatum ROI with an appropriately reported voxel cluster. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12b, FSL) are reported. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (IAPS images paired with alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage pictures). The study reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcoholic versus non-alcoholic beverage cues (both alcohol>non-alcohol and non-alcohol>alcohol contrasts) and provides group-level voxelwise statistical maps with family-wise error cluster correction and reported clusters/tables. Results are presented in figures/tables and VOI follow-ups; methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing steps, and analysis software (AFNI). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI task contrasts with qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results.

This empirical fMRI study uses visual smoking-related and affective images and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral, positive>neutral, negative>neutral) entered into group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM8). Results are reported voxelwise with coordinates and cluster statistics within an anatomical mask (small-volume approach) with cluster correction, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (ISIS images) in a within-subjects randomized crossover design. The authors report within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain results (uncorrected p<0.001, cluster threshold 10) and provide coordinates/tables and figures. MRI field strength (1.5T), stimuli, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Participant sex/mean age are not fully reported (preferred per I7 but not required). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in alcohol-dependent patients and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction. The paper includes within-participant cue contrasts such as [alcohol pull > soft drink pull] with peak coordinates and FWE SVC-corrected p-values in mPFC (and SVC results in NAcc), reports MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM8), and participant characteristics (male alcohol-dependent inpatients). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Exclude because the experimental cue modality is individualized script-driven guided imagery (auditory/imaginal), not visual cues. The review requires studies with a clear visual cue component (I3), which this study does not provide. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts: alcohol cue > neutral-relaxing reported), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with familywise correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (visual cue component). Exclusion criteria met: none []. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports ROI-based analyses (extraction of COPEs from 14 a priori ROIs) and does not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues – food images), I4 (within-participant contrast: food vs. object/baseline). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC results reported), I6 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of qualifying results provided). I7: participant demographics, cue type, and software are reported though field strength is not explicitly stated (missing detail does not override exclusion). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not provide the required voxelwise task-evoked results for inclusion in the voxelwise meta-analysis.

This fMRI study examines appetitive (natural food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures + tones paired with liquid food) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing CS+ > CS−. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction (amygdala, NAcc, vmPFC) at FWE-corrected thresholds, satisfying the requirement for a task-evoked voxelwise result. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, Matlab) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual cigarette and food cues and reports group-level voxelwise (whole-brain and ROI-thresholded) task-evoked results; however, it does not present a within-participant cue>control (drug cues > neutral/control or natural reward cues > neutral/control) contrast. The analyses focus on regulation contrasts (LATER vs NOW) and cue type comparisons (cigarette vs food) but no drug-cue vs control-stimulus contrast or neutral baseline is reported. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study reports resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity (DLPFC seed) comparing alcohol dependence (AD) and internet gaming disorder (IGD) during abstinence; it does not implement a task-based cue-reactivity paradigm with visual cues nor a within-participant cue>control contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without task-evoked results) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrasts; only between-group comparisons). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (no drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with clear visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (no task-evoked whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (no task-evoked voxelwise coordinates available). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study should be EXCLUDED from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (International Smoking Image Series). It reports within-subject contrasts (smoking cue > neutral cue) with whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (FDR-corrected results) and provides coordinates/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8, FSL) and detailed methods are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines visual food cues (natural rewards) with fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but it does not provide a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control (non-reward) stimuli. All stimuli are high-calorie food pictures and contrasts are between cognitive-regulation conditions (up-regulation, suppression, reappraisal) and passive viewing of the same food cues rather than food>neutral or cue>non-cue contrasts. Therefore I4 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (acceptable reporting formats), I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4. No exclusion criteria from the list are directly triggered. Full text appears complete.

This article is excluded because it does not report task-based fMRI voxelwise results for visual drug or natural reward cue-reactivity. The paper is a symposium summarizing human laboratory studies (IV alcohol self-administration, taste tests, HPA-axis measures, and clinical assessments) and while it briefly notes that an fMRI study investigated neural correlates of stress and alcohol-context cues, the full text provides no fMRI methods, no visual cue fMRI task description, and no within-participant drug-cue>control voxelwise results (whole-brain or SVC). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI study assessing visual cue-reactivity), I4 (no within-participant cue>control fMRI contrast reported), I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results). Exclusion criteria met: none of the specified exclusion IDs (E3–E6) directly apply, but failure to meet required inclusion criteria leads to exclusion. Full text appears complete for the presented experiments (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses visual smoking-related cues and neutral pictures during task fMRI and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs neutral cues. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain 2×2 ANOVA with FWE correction and tables/figures of coordinates), satisfying voxelwise task-evoked reporting. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study investigates fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts (fattening > nonfattening), and it provides participant demographics and imaging/preprocessing details. However, the fMRI results are reported using ROI-based averages and ICCs across a priori ROIs rather than presenting any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (no coordinates or voxelwise SVC results are reported). Thus it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (high- and low-calorie images) as natural reward stimuli, with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie>objects; low-calorie>objects) and group-level voxelwise analyses. The authors report small-volume-corrected voxelwise results within a priori ROIs with FWE correction, and provide coordinates/psc extraction details. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore all inclusion criteria for a visual-cue task-evoked voxelwise result are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-evoked BOLD fMRI responses to visual food cues (images of milkshake vs water) with within-participant contrasts (anticipatory milkshake cue > anticipatory tasteless-solution cue and receipt contrasts). Analyses were conducted as group-level voxelwise whole-brain tests (cluster-level q-FDR < 0.05) and report anatomical locations and peak coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens Allegra 3T), preprocessing, and SPM12 software. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI task using visual Pavlovian cues (colored lights predicting snack foods), satisfying natural reward-related visual cueing (I3). It includes within-subject contrasts of CS+ > CS− (general PIT) and specific PIT contrasts (I4). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (FWE-corrected, coordinates/tables provided and results archived on NeuroVault), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (I5, I6). Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), meeting reporting preferences (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not assess drug or natural reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues. The fMRI task is a real-time smoking decision paradigm with stress manipulations (working-memory load, shock probability) and in-scanner e-cigarette delivery, not a visual drug-cue>control stimulus contrast. Although the paper reports whole-brain analyses and provides participant/MRI details (I5, I6, I7 satisfied), it fails to meet I3 (visual cue-related drug/natural reward reactivity) and I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control or natural reward>control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking-cue videos and matched control videos, with within-subject contrasts of smoking>control at first level and a group-level random-effects voxelwise analysis (FLAME) with permutation-based TFCE correction (P<0.05). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise activations (figures and supplementary table) and include participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (videos), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, lack of within-subject cue>control contrast, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This article is a non-empirical narrative review summarizing fMRI and MRS findings across multiple studies rather than reporting original human fMRI data. It does not present an original within-participant drug-cue>control (or natural reward>control) voxelwise group-level contrast, nor does it report primary whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical coordinates/results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an original fMRI cue-reactivity study with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control analysis presented), I5 (no qualifying voxelwise group-level task-evoked result), I6 (no primary voxelwise coordinates/results available in this paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods describing review process, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using pictorial (visual) smoking cues and neutral controls, reporting within-subject contrasts comparing smoking versus neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP) and cue-exposure-corrected contrasts (LCSP minus PNSP). Group-level voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates and Z-values (whole-brain voxelwise results reported at p<0.001 uncorrected). Imaging parameters (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM5), and participant demographics are provided. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with preprocessing/statistics details. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food pictures > neutral/non-food images or baseline); the reported contrasts compare different task instructions (inhibition, imaginary eating, passive viewing) applied to the same food stimuli rather than cue versus control stimuli. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant food>neutral contrast images entered into group-level analyses. The paper reports voxelwise, hypothesis-driven small-volume-corrected results in the ventral striatum (familywise error–corrected) and also an exploratory whole-brain one-sample t test (FWE-corrected), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Results are presented in figures and tables (statistical parametric maps, scatterplots, and tables of activations). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking cues (images) and reports within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts. The paper conducted group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise threshold p<0.005 with cluster extent correction determined by Monte Carlo) and reports significant clusters (baseline one-sample t-test and Time × Stimulation interactions with cluster results and figures/tables). Key details (participant age range, sex distribution, cue type, MRI field strength 1.5T, and preprocessing/statistical software SPM12) are provided. Thus the study satisfies the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity fMRI with qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results and sufficient reporting to extract coordinates/activation loci. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of amphetamine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual film clips. It reports a within-participant contrast (Drug movies > Neutral movies) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain FWE-corrected activations. Methods report MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), participant age/sex, and cue type. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-evoked fMRI studies of drug-related reward cues.

This is an empirical human fMRI study that uses clear visual reward cues (image of a $100 bill vs a blurry rectangle) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing reward vs nonreward (main effect of reward). Imaging analyses are group-level voxelwise, whole-brain (z>3.1, cluster-corrected p<.05) with results presented in text, tables and figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking videos (developmentally appropriate dynamic visual cues) and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral) at the group level. The paper describes whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports peak coordinates and z-statistics (e.g., NAcc and DLPFC peaks), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain). MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), participant ages, cue type, and task details are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food pictures (spicy vs non-spicy) as cues (natural reward). It reports within-subject spicy>non-spicy contrast and group-level voxelwise results corrected at p<0.05 FWE with coordinates and cluster thresholds, and provides details on participants, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing and statistical software. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or absence of within-participant cue>control contrast) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis of visual cue-related fMRI studies of drug/natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly used visual alcohol cues (90 pictures of alcoholic and neutral beverages) and generated within-subject contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages) at the individual level, with group-level statistical maps computed for each contrast. The authors report whole-brain voxelwise analyses and report clusters related to alcohol-cue responses (e.g., anterior cingulate) and reference Supplementary Table T1 for alcohol-related findings, satisfying the requirement that qualifying voxelwise results are available. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain/small-volume-corrected result), I6 (acceptable reporting of voxelwise results in tables/supplement) and I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and software) are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing hedonic and utilitarian food images to control objects (e.g., H>U, U>O). Analyses include group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistics with whole-brain random-effects analysis (SPM2) and multiple-comparison correction (FDR P=0.05); coordinates/region results are described. MRI field strength (3.0 T), participant age/sex, cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual drug (cocaine) and natural reward (sexual) cues using a backward-masking visual paradigm in human participants. It reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine vs neutral; sex vs neutral) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps using SPM2 (voxelwise t maps, cluster-corrected p-values reported). Imaging parameters (3T scanner), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), participant age/sex and cue types are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked results of visual reward-cue reactivity and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant task contrasts comparing food versus non-food images and high-calorie versus low-calorie images. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with stringent whole-brain FWE cluster correction and also uses small-volume ROI corrections for a priori regions, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or SVC-corrected evidence. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of analyses and results.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking-related vs. neutral stimuli and reports a group-level voxelwise contrast (smoking cue > control cue) entered into a random-effects ANOVA. Analyses were conducted within an ROI mask and significant activations (with peak coordinates) are reported for the cue>control contrast. The paper includes MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing software (SPM8), and participant demographics. Although the ROI-constrained analyses used an uncorrected threshold (p<0.001, k=20), the study nonetheless provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results within a defined mask and reports coordinate data, which meets the review’s requirement for voxelwise results (acceptable via small-volume/ROI-constrained reporting per I6). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (chocolate) cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (chocolate pictures) and neutral control pictures. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of chocolate>neutral and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses, with cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo) and reported clusters/ROIs predicting subsequent intake. Scanner field strength (3T), participant demographics (female undergraduates), stimuli, and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are described. Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study using visual food cues (natural rewards) in a within-subjects design. The study modeled task-evoked responses to food image trials (healthy and unhealthy) and conducted group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (3dMVM) reporting significant clusters with MNI coordinates and extracted beta-values, satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Visual stimuli were the Food-pics images and participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, ANTs, SPSS) are reported. The within-participant design included condition contrasts (go/no-go trial types and collapsed food trials versus habitual/restricted sleep baseline), providing within-subject cue-related contrasts. Therefore I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity (drug reward) that includes a clear visual cue component (participants held and viewed a cigarette via live video feed). The authors report within-subject contrasts comparing cigarette versus control cues (main effect of cue; cigarette>control) and present group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates and cluster-correction thresholds (whole-brain analyses reported in tables and figures). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL, etc.), and participant demographics (male, ages 18–45). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual Pavlovian cues and food images. The paper reports within-participant voxelwise cue>control contrasts (food-outcome cues vs. no-outcome cue) during the task, with group-level, small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical results and reported coordinates. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion decision: The paper does not report any task-evoked voxelwise cue-reactivity contrast (e.g., drug-cues > control stimuli) at the group level. Although the study used visual smoking images during an in-scanner pleasantness rating task (behavioral cue exposure), the reported fMRI voxelwise results are for an interoceptive attention task (interoception vs exteroception) and for resting-state/seed connectivity analyses. Therefore it lacks the required within-participant cue>control task-evoked voxelwise result. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (no qualifying task-evoked cue-reactivity voxelwise result alongside connectivity analyses) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study using visual smoking cues) and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli) and I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked result for cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Thus the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of food versus nonfood (food>nonfood) at the group level, with voxelwise analyses using small-volume correction (SVC, FWE-corrected) and reported peak coordinates and statistics. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 GLM pipeline, participant age/sex, and cue types. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural reward) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results, but it does not present a within-participant cue>control contrast of natural reward-related cues versus control stimuli. Instead, the reported contrasts compare cognitive reappraisal/suppression instructions (e.g., costs of eating > imagine eating; benefits of not eating > imagine eating; suppress craving > imagine eating). Although these are within-subject contrasts, they reflect strategy effects rather than a straightforward cue-reactivity contrast (appetizing food cues > control/unappetizing/baseline) required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain corrected results), I6 (voxelwise results reported), I7 (reporting age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/software). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I4 (no within-participant natural reward-cues > control-stimuli contrast reported). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of cue-reactivity to e-cigarette stimuli that includes a clear visual cue component (images of the e-cigarettes with colored bands) and within-participant contrasts comparing exposed/drug-related cues to control e-cigarettes. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with small-volume-corrected (SVC) statistics in the nucleus accumbens (e.g., p_SVC values) and whole-brain correlations (coordinates reported), satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of methamphetamine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with a within-participant Methamphetamine Cue > Control Cue contrast. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with cluster-corrected Z-statistic maps and a table of coordinates (satisfying whole-brain voxelwise result requirements). Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), and participant demographics (age/sex) are included. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue-based task-evoked whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity studies.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual-only stimuli (food video paradigm) with within-subject contrasts of food-video (FV) epochs versus control-video epochs. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 with family-wise-error voxelwise correction (P<0.05) and reporting of activation clusters (coordinates referenced, Table 2), fulfilling whole-brain/small-volume-corrected evidence requirements. Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 4-Tesla MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (hedonic food images vs neutral non-food images). It includes within-participant contrasts (hedonic food > nonfood) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise threshold p<0.01 with cluster-level FDR correction), with tables/figures of coordinates and t-values. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual smoking vs neutral images (meets I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral and reports analyses based on those contrasts (meets I4). The paper reports a group-level voxel-wise analysis restricted to the PCC (cluster-level correction using nonparametric permutation testing), which constitutes a small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result (meets I5 and I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported (meets I7). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no reliance solely on ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses, and it is empirical). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using clear visual cues (colored circles predicting monetary gains/losses) to index natural reward-related cue-reactivity. The design includes within-participant contrasts (anticipation/delivery of gains vs losses and cue-related responses vs baseline in ROI analyses), and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (vmPFC and other a priori masks) and coordinate-based findings. Core methods (participants, cue type, MRI field strength = 3T, AFNI preprocessing/statistics) and full results are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met: results include voxelwise task-evoked analyses (so E3 and E4 not applicable) and include within-participant cue contrasts (so E5 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study meets inclusion for fMRI visual cue-reactivity of a natural reward and provides qualifying small-volume-corrected voxelwise results.

This is a human fMRI study using visual smoking stimuli with within-subject contrasts (smoking minus matched control teeth-brushing stimuli: e.g., BEGIN: S2-T2; END: S4-T4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (second-level SPM analyses, tables of activations/deactivations and coordinates across brain regions; ROI and whole-brain results described). Methods report participant age/sex composition, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study of drug-cue reactivity using visual stimuli (drug-related pictures) with incarcerated adolescent substance users. The main within-participant contrast (drug-related pictures > neutral pictures) is reported at the group level with whole-brain results (p < .05, FWE corrected) and additional voxelwise/ROI results and tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked cue>control analyses using visual cues. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text reports an fMRI task with visual smoking vs. non-smoking video cues (visual stimuli) and within-participant contrasts (smoking > non-smoking) during abstinence. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (FSL FLAME1, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05), and trial-by-trial parametric voxelwise analyses and conjunctions are also presented. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. The manuscript includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue reactivity using a clear visual cue (participants viewed a cigarette via live video feed while holding it). The paper reports a within-participant voxelwise contrast of cigarette cue > control cue (voxel-wise paired t-test) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical results (cluster-corrected), with activation coordinates/regions described. Preprocessing and analysis software (AFNI, FSL, AIR, NIS) and scanner field strength (3-Tesla) are reported. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity using visual drug cues and reports qualifying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a clear food>nonfood contrast. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (drink x cue interaction; cluster-corrected maps) and ROI analyses, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), stimulus details, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-based task-evoked voxelwise results and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking cues (images) with a within-participant contrast (smoking cues > neutral cues). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed using SPM8 with whole-brain FDR-corrected results reported (tables/figures/coordinate reporting present). Methods report participants (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is original human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (happy faces) and neutral control (calm faces). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of happy>calm and other within-participant contrasts, with group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain correction for most contrasts and a small-volume-corrected voxelwise age effect within a striatum mask) and peak coordinates provided. Participant demographics, cue types, scanner field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images in adolescents. The task includes within-participant contrasts of appetizing versus plain food stimuli (choice trials), and group- and within-group voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with appropriate multiple-comparison correction (FWE within-group; FDR whole-brain for between-group), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Key methodological details (age/sex, cue types, 3.0T MRI, SPM8 preprocessing) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group without within-subject cue>control, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (actual foods presented) as natural reward stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts of food > non-food. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (with tables/figures of coordinates and a reported voxelwise threshold and cluster extent) and also a region-of-interest confirmation for the hypothalamus (small-volume approach). Participant details (sex distribution), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies. Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. The study reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs. objects, low-calorie vs. objects, high vs. low) and performs an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects analysis with cluster-level correction (FSL FEAT/LME), fulfilling the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. Results and contrasts are described in the main text and figures/tables. Participant age/sex and cue type and the analysis software (FSL/FEAT) are reported; MRI field strength is not stated but missing reporting alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The full text reports an fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (participants held a cigarette and viewed a live video feed), includes within-subject cigarette>control contrasts, and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical results with tables of coordinates and figures. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL, etc.). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of daily smokers using visual smoking cues during a probed-recall task. The full text reports within-participant contrasts comparing smoking-cue trials to control (and neutral) trials, whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster-wise correction, and tables/coordinates of significant clusters (e.g., rIFG). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are reported. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural reward stimuli (romantic IAPS images) with within-participant contrasts (romantic > neutral) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM8; cluster-corrected via 3dClustSim). Scanner field strength (3T), participant age/sex (female, 18–25), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7.

This fMRI study examines visual food cue-reactivity (natural reward) and includes within-participant food>control contrasts, but it reports only ROI- and system-level ROI voxel-parameter extractions (e.g., VS/OFC ROI beta estimates and aggregated ROI system means) rather than group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise analyses with coordinates/clusters). Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise group-level result. (a) Exclusion criterion met: E3. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant food>control contrast), I7 (participant sex/age, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise result), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in main text/tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given these points, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures vs scrambled control), with a within-subject design reporting food>control contrasts. Group-level voxelwise results are reported: a small-volume-corrected (SVC) hypothalamic effect (pFWE-corr reported) and exploratory whole-brain task-evoked results and figures/tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and analysis details (GLM/PPI, thresholds, software for behavioral stats) are provided in the full text. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I3) visual cues, (I4) within-participant cue>control contrast, (I5) qualifying voxelwise SVC/whole-brain results, and (I6) availability of voxelwise results in the main text/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (whole-brain flexible factorial and two-sample t tests, with figures/tables of coordinates), and preprocessing/MRI field strength/statistical software (3.0T, SPM8) and participant age/sex are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: (I3) It is a task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie and low-calorie food photographs vs brick walls). (I4) It includes within-participant contrasts of food cues > control stimuli (high-calorie foods minus brick walls). (I5) It reports group-level voxelwise, task-evoked statistical results from a second-level flexible factorial whole-brain analysis with cluster-level correction (spatial extent p<0.05 after whole-brain correction) and voxelwise statistics reported; results are provided in tables/figures. (I6) Voxelwise results are reported and presented in figures/tables. (I7) Participant demographics (age/sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria applied: [I3,I4,I5,I6,I7]. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an empirical fMRI study using arterial-spin-labeling perfusion fMRI with visual smoking-related vs. neutral pictures. It reports within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral), and a whole-brain voxelwise group × cue ANOVA with FWE-corrected clusters (task-evoked voxelwise results). Participant demographics, cue type, scanner details, and preprocessing/statistics are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis eligibility for visual cue-based task fMRI with qualifying voxelwise results.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of appetizing vs bland foods). It includes a within-subject contrast of appetizing>bland foods, reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-group SPM{t} maps and small-volume-corrected FWE results) with peak coordinates in tables/figures, and provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (9-s video clips). It includes within-participant contrasts of sexual (explicit) cues > control (non-sexual exciting) cues and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: whole-brain FWE-corrected activations for explicit>exciting and small-volume-corrected (SVC) FWE results (ventral striatum, dACC, amygdala, substantia nigra) with peak coordinates and p-values. Participant demographics, cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (hedonic food > non-food and hedonic food > neutral food) and group-level voxelwise results. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholding reported, cluster/voxel statistics and coordinates) and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis (fusiform). Participant characteristics (sex, ages), cue types, scanner field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (high- vs low-caloric images) and reports within-subject contrasts (high-caloric > low-caloric). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (SPM12; voxel threshold p<0.001 with cluster FWE correction reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. Participant details (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of hedonic food images vs neutral non-food objects (H>O) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM5) with FDR correction; small-volume corrections (ROIs) are also used. Results are presented in the main text and figures with voxelwise statistics and t-values. Participant demographics (age range, sex counts), cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using validated visual food images. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (fattening food > objects; fattening > nonfattening) and group comparisons, with group-level voxelwise analyses: ROI-based small-volume correction across a preselected extended satiety network (FWE cluster correction across ROIs) and exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-thresholded). Results are reported anatomically and with corrected voxelwise statistics/cluster maps and described coordinates/regions. Participant demographics, cue type, and imaging/analysis approaches are described in the methods (with further acquisition/processing detail in supplements). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-cue images (I3). The methods describe within-subject contrasts (methamphetamine task vs rest baseline) and one-sample t tests within the patient group, i.e., a within-participant cue>control analysis (I4). Group-level voxelwise statistical analysis was performed using SPM5 with a voxelwise threshold (T=3.11, P<.001 uncorrected) and cluster extent threshold, indicating a group-level task-evoked voxelwise result (I5). The paper’s main text reports voxelwise activation maps and regional findings (anterior cingulate, frontal lobe), satisfying the allowance for results presented in text/figures/tables (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported (I7). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; core content appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this fMRI study clearly assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3) and includes a within-participant contrast of Food > Non-Food control images (I4), and reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength and preprocessing software (I7), the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (either whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). The analyses rely on ROI-based extraction and regressions; no qualifying voxelwise group results or corrected voxelwise tables/coordinates are provided. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC task-evoked result), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study investigates neural responses to favorite-food (natural reward), stress, and neutral cues using personalized guided-imagery scripts delivered via audio (auditory-only cues), not visual stimuli. Meta-analysis requires a clear visual cue component (I3), which is not satisfied. The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts of favorite-food>neutral and other condition contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with FWE correction), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper is excluded solely because it fails I3 (no visual cue component).

This fMRI study directly addresses natural (sexual) reward-related cue-reactivity using visual cues (predictive pictograms) and visual erotic rewards. The task modeled cue and reward phases including a control (non-reward) cue, permitting within-participant contrasts of erotic-cue versus control conditions. Group-level voxelwise ROI results survived small-volume FWE correction (PSVC-FWE<0.05) in the ventral striatum and are reported in the main text/figures, satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics (male, ages), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), task design, and basic preprocessing/statistical approaches are reported (with further preprocessing details in Supplement). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E5) apply: results are not limited to uncorrected ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only analyses, or solely between-group contrasts without within-subject cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images) and includes a within-participant contrast (high-calorie food > nonfood). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results within predefined regions of interest with family-wise error–corrected voxelwise clusters in the insula (i.e., small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of food (natural reward) cue reactivity using visual stimuli and includes a within-participant contrast of food cues > control images (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the manuscript, as provided, reports IFG parameter estimates extracted from a 6-mm spherical ROI and group-level ROI-based analyses; while whole-brain contrast images were generated for second-level analysis, no voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level statistical results (e.g., cluster coordinates or SVC-corrected voxels) are reported in the supplied text. Therefore the paper appears to present only ROI-extracted results and lacks a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise (whole-brain or SVC) result required by I5. This meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported voxelwise whole-brain or SVC group-level results). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual stimuli (photographs) and within-participant contrasts of high-energy-dense (high-ED) > low-ED food cues. Group-level voxelwise second-level analyses were performed (SPM8) with whole-brain thresholding/cluster correction reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical methods are described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts).

This is an empirical fMRI study in treatment-seeking smokers who viewed smoking and neutral images (visual cues) and provided within-subject contrasts (LookSmoking > LookNeutral). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain cluster correction (AlphaSim) and peak coordinates/clusters are presented in tables/figures. MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant characteristics are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI task study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-participant contrasts of highly palatable cues > control stimuli (high vs. moderate; high vs. neutral). The manuscript describes whole-brain analyses (used as a proof-of-probe) and voxelwise ROI analyses with cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo/3dClustSim within anatomically defined ROI masks), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (small-volume-corrected). Relevant results are reported in main text and Supporting Information (figures/tables). Participant demographics and cue type are reported; some acquisition details (e.g., field strength) appear in Supporting Information but missing here would not preclude inclusion per criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This paper reports an fMRI task with visual natural-reward (high-calorie food) cues (meets I3) and provides participant and scanner details (meets I7). However, the full text presents only seed-based task-dependent connectivity (PPI) results comparing oxytocin vs placebo and does not report a within-participant task-evoked cue>control voxelwise activation contrast (e.g., high-calorie > non-food) nor provide group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation maps/coordinates in this manuscript. Although the authors reference prior BOLD results from the same dataset, those task-evoked activations are not reported here as qualifying voxelwise results. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria not met in this full text: I4 and I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I7.

This is an event-related task fMRI study using visual heroin-related and neutral images (24 each) and reports within-subject heroin-related > neutral contrasts. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (AFNI Monte Carlo simulation) and results are presented in figures/tables. Methods include MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (DPARSF, SPM8, AFNI), participant demographics (male subjects; demographic table referenced), and cue type. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses) are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (500 color images of high- and low-calorie foods and non-food controls). It includes within-participant contrasts (HiCal vs Control, LoCal vs Control, Food vs Control, HiCal vs LoCal). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using a region-of-interest approach with small-volume correction (SVC) in SPM8 (FDR-corrected), and coordinates/results are described (supplementary tables noted). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) are reported. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual methamphetamine-related stimuli. The paper reports within-participant MA > neutral cue contrasts and presents whole-brain, voxel-wise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected) derived with FSL and BROCCOLI (baseline MA vs. neutral produced significant clusters in vmPFC, caudate, etc.). MRI field strength (3T), cue type (MA-related images), participant demographics, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it meets I3 (visual cue fMRI cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results presented in figures/tables), and I7 (key methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in smokers using visual cigarette-related stimuli (graphic warning labels) and measuring cue-elicited craving and recognition. It includes within-participant contrasts of LABEL>CONTROL and HIGH>LOW, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (thresholded and cluster-corrected) with tables and figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (audio-visual smoking videos). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking control stimuli (SCs vs non-SCs), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using ROI-based voxelwise analyses with statistical thresholds and cluster correction; coordinates and cluster statistics are reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8, ASL toolbox) are described. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI-only results, only connectivity/resting-state, or non-empirical) are met. Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (high- vs low-calorie images) to probe natural reward cue-reactivity. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., high-calorie go > low-calorie go; nogo > go), and group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses with whole-brain cluster correction (Z>2.3, p<0.05). Results are reported in figures/tables with ROIs and coordinate clusters, and methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics (FSL). The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (high-energy vs. neutral; low-energy vs. neutral; high vs. low). Second-level group random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with whole-brain FDR thresholds and cluster criteria (and interaction contrasts), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Imaging field strength (3T), preprocessing (DPARSF) and statistical software (SPM12) and participant characteristics (female sample, BMI range) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.
