This empirical fMRI study used visual advertisements (images) of e-cigarettes and control images, testing cue-reactivity in young adults. It includes within-subject contrasts between flavored/tobacco e-cigarette cues and control stimuli, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster FWE-corrected) and ROI analyses (NAc), and provides necessary methodological details (participant demographics, cue type, 3T scanner, SPM12 preprocessing). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (subliminal sexual images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (Sex vs Neutral; Sex vs Fixation) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses for main effects and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis in the NAcc). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (FDA graphic warning images vs non-graphic controls). It includes within-participant contrasts (graphic > non-graphic, graphic > baseline, non-graphic > baseline) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with cluster-based correction and coordinate tables (small-volume/ROI-corrected analyses are described). Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software FSL) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food and sexual images) with within-participant contrasts (food>baseline, sexual scenes>baseline). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain regression analyses linking neural responses to behavioral outcomes (BMI change and sexual desire) with stereotactic coordinates and statistical thresholds (e.g., p<0.001), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Core methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T scanner field strength, preprocessing and SPM2 software). There is also ROI work, but the presence of whole-brain voxelwise results avoids exclusion for ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual cues paired with monetary outcomes (natural reward). The task uses clearly defined visual cues for gain, loss, bivalent, and neutral outcomes. The analysis includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., gain vs. neutral, loss vs. neutral; anticipation and outcome models) and reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain voxelwise ANOVAs with cluster tables, Tables 5–6), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise, group-level task-evoked statistics. Voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T scanners), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL, R) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an original human fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual sexual (and monetary) stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing Sexual (and Monetary) cues/outcomes versus Neutral (e.g., CS+Sex/CS+Mon vs CS−) in task-evoked analyses. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain cluster FWE-corrected statistics and coordinates, and small-volume-corrected (SVC FWE) results are also presented. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant characteristics (male, heterosexual) and cue types are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and the preferred-reported-detail I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos of foods), with within-participant contrasts of food>objects (e.g., [F–O], [UF–O], [HF–O]) performed at the group level. The paper reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses and whole-brain results (p<.05 FWE cluster-corrected) and ROI/masked analyses, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Results are presented in the main text with contrasts and ROI/whole-brain findings. Participant demographics, cue types, preprocessing/statistical software (SPM, GLM) and behavioral/task details are reported; MRI field strength is not evident in the provided text but this alone does not exclude the study. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (high-calorie food) cue-reactivity that used a multimodal cue presentation (gustatory tastes delivered concurrently with visual instructions), satisfying the requirement for a visual cue component. The analysis includes a within-participant contrast of high-calorie cues > water (control). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported (FLAME, cluster-corrected p-values, peak coordinates), and supplementary/peak data are referenced. Preprocessing and analysis software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME), MRI field strength (3T), participant age range, and cue type are reported. Although sex breakdown is not explicitly stated in the provided text, the meta-analysis notes that missing such details alone should not exclude a qualifying study. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (explicit sexual images). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing sexual>neutral pictures (Sex LO > Neutral LO; Sex PC > Neutral PC). Group-level voxelwise second-level analyses were performed and reported with small-volume/FWE-corrected ROI results; whole-brain analyses are referenced in the supplementary material. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

While this is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (images) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (premature > correct contrasts) and provides figures/tables and acquisition/preprocessing details, it does NOT report a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (neutral) stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli. The primary reported within-subject contrasts are ‘premature > correct’ within incentive contexts rather than a simple drug-cue > neutral-cue contrast. Because inclusion criterion I4 (a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli or natural reward > control contrast) is not met, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis despite meeting other criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of sexual (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual pornography stimuli. The experiment includes within-subject contrasts of explicit (pornographic) > neutral pictures, and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (GLM whole-brain analyses with FWE cluster/peak correction). Methods report participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual reward-cue fMRI studies and does not trigger exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria applied: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an fMRI study of visual food (natural reward) cues (meets I3). However, the manuscript reports ROI-based analyses (extraction of mean ROI beta values and behavioral correlations) rather than group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected contrasts. The paper does not present qualifying voxelwise food>control or cue>control group-level maps/SMC results in the main text or supplements, and the primary reported contrasts are between food conditions (Large vs Small) within ROIs. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result (I5) and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear reported within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast available for meta-analysis) and I5 (no qualifying voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images: high-energy desserts and low-energy vegetables). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (one-sample t-tests on pre-vs-post contrast images) with coordinates/cluster results, acquired on a 3T scanner and analyzed with SPM12/DARTEL. It includes within-participant cue-related contrasts (nogo_dessert vs rest and nogo_vegetable vs rest, and pre-post difference contrasts) which satisfy the requirement for cue>control contrasts. Participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required for eligibility. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies.

This study should be excluded because it reports only ROI-based analyses and does not present any group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). The authors extracted mean signals across anatomically defined ROIs and report ROI-level statistics without reporting voxelwise SPM results or SVC-corrected coordinates. Exclusion criterion met: E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food cues), I4 (within-participant contrast hedonic > neutral foods), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues and reports within-participant contrasts (smoking-related vs neutral) with task-evoked voxelwise results. The paper reports both whole-brain corrected analyses and small-volume-corrected (SVC) voxelwise results (e.g., DLPFC, amygdala) and ROI/NAcc analyses, with thresholds and cluster correction described. Methods (3.0T scanner, AFNI processing), cue types, and participant group descriptions are provided in the full text. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue reactivity with qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts and group-level voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual stimuli (images of stimulant drugs, food, neutral items) in an event-related cue reactivity task, satisfying the visual-cue requirement. The authors report within-participant contrasts (drug vs neutral, food vs neutral, drug vs food) and present group-level voxelwise statistical results via whole-brain analyses with cluster-level correction (AFNI 3dClustSim) and VOI analyses; results and coordinates/tables are reported in the main text and supplementary materials. These elements meet inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results. MRI field strength is not specified in the excerpt (a preferred but non-exclusionary detail). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study in smokers using visual cigarette-related cues (colored squares and cigarette images) and a within-subject cue manipulation. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing CS+ versus CS− (e.g., Attend CS+ vs Attend CS− with significant effects) and group-level random-effects voxelwise statistical maps (thresholded at p<0.001 uncorrected) and ROI follow-up around peak voxels. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM5/FSL) are reported. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise cue-reactivity with visual stimuli. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual monetary cues (ring of dollar signs/blue pound signs) to probe reward-related cue reactivity in abstinent smokers vs. non-smokers. The design includes a within-subject contrast of reward vs. neutral (incentive) trials and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain cluster-corrected maps with reported peak coordinates in ventral striatum, precentral sulcus/FEF, parietal lobules, ACC, PCC). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3.0T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, AFNI). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI with visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie > low-calorie food images, meeting I3 and I4. However, the paper reports ROI-extracted mean z-scores and group-level t-tests on those ROI values rather than presenting group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected), and no voxelwise coordinates or corrected group maps are provided. Therefore it fails I5 (no qualifying voxelwise group-level result) and I6 (no voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures as qualifying group-level statistics). This matches exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses without qualifying voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (erotic images). It reports within-participant contrasts (erotic cue > control and monetary cue > control) at the group level, with voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-level corrected across the whole brain, coordinates and figures provided). Participant/sample, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. These features satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provide qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I3 is not met: the cue modality used is gustatory (taste of alcohol vs. juice) rather than a visual cue, so the study does not assess visual cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (the study uses within-participant alcohol cue > control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain analyses are reported), I6 (voxelwise results are presented in the main text/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Exclusion criteria: none met (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual sexual cues (natural reward) in Parkinson’s patients. It reports within-participant contrasts (sexual cues > neutral and sexual cues > other rewards), provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with FDR correction and peak coordinates, and also reports small-volume/ROI analyses. Methods (3 T scanner, SPM preprocessing/statistics) and participant details are provided in the full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cues (BEGIN/END images) with both smokers and non-smokers. The authors report within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control stimuli (e.g., BEGIN-smoking minus BEGIN-control) and group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME group analyses) with FWE-corrected voxelwise thresholds reported; coordinates and statistical maps are presented in tables/figures. MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing and statistical software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME) and participant demographics (n=16 per group, sexes, ages similar) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of visual food (natural reward) cues with group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results and adequate reporting, but it does not include a within-participant cue>control (food>neutral/non-reward) contrast required by I4. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI natural reward visual cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results reported), I6 (voxelwise results and coordinates reported), I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli; contrasts are high vs low calorie and available vs unavailable, but no food vs non-food/neutral contrast). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I4.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (high- and low-calorie food images) with explicit within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs fixation, low-calorie vs fixation, neutral vs fixation). Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses are reported for predefined ROIs (coordinates, cluster sizes, and statistical thresholds are provided and summarized in tables/figures), which satisfies the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results. Relevant methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength = 3T, preprocessing/software = SPM5) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity and reports qualifying voxelwise results (ROIs defined with WFU Pickatlas and voxelwise regressions reported), and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue-reactivity using visual food images (high- and low-calorie) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs. object; low-calorie vs. object) in premeal/postmeal states. Group-level random-effects voxelwise GLM results are reported with Talairach coordinates, cluster thresholds, and FDR correction (i.e., qualifying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). Results are reported in figures and coordinate tables. Methodological details (4.0T scanner, BrainVoyager preprocessing/statistics, cue types) are provided and the full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity and provides voxelwise task-evoked group results appropriate for meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual package images (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (viewing/tasting conditions minus rest; package-type contrasts and congruent vs incongruent package-taste contrasts), satisfying a cue>control contrast (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported via exploratory whole-brain analyses and an ROI-based voxelwise approach with cluster-size family-wise error correction across the analysis mask (small-volume approach), meeting the requirement for whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results (I5). The text indicates coordinate/cluster results and supplementary materials/figures are available (I6). Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and this is primary empirical human fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study examines neural responses to chocolate-related decision-making and reports group-level voxelwise results (including whole-brain exploratory analyses) and provides participant age/sex, cue type (chocolate), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing software (SPM8), it does not assess classic cue-reactivity (i.e., passive exposure to reward cues vs. control cues) using a visual cue-reactivity paradigm. The experimental manipulation is a chocolate-specific delay-discounting decision task (difficult vs. easy decisions) rather than a within-participant cue>control stimulus contrast (e.g., food cue > neutral cue). Therefore it fails to meet I3 (fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component in the sense of cue-reactivity) and I4 (at least one within-participant cue>control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) and fearful social scenes. It reports within-subject contrasts of erotic>neutral (task-evoked) at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise results (p<0.05 FWE-corrected) and ROI/SVC results also reported. Visual cue stimuli (IAPS erotic pictures) are clearly used. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visually presented labels as cues. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs low-calorie and vs neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction (whole-brain inference). Methods report participant demographics, scanner (3T), and preprocessing/software (SPM8). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (appetizing food) using visual stimuli and task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Participants viewed food images (visual cues) and group-level contrasts reported include food viewing (Close + Far) > fixation baseline and regulation contrasts (Far > Close); results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise statistics (SPM8; tables referenced: S1–S8) and coordinate tables/figures are provided. Participant characteristics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses, and it includes within-participant cue (food) > control (baseline/fixation) contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual natural rewards.

Exclusion applied: E4 (study reports only resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses and does not report any task-evoked fMRI cue>control contrast) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control task contrast is provided). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (although the study includes visual food images for craving ratings, these images were not presented during task fMRI; the fMRI data are resting-state), I4 (no within-participant cue>control task contrast reported), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported — only resting-state connectivity voxelwise results), I6 (not applicable because task-evoked voxelwise results are absent). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for a task-evoked visual cue-reactivity contrast and must be excluded.

The study is a human fMRI experiment using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (voxelwise thresholds with cluster correction), and provides participant and acquisition details. Thus it meets I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results reported in main text), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4). The reported contrasts compare the same food images under two labeling conditions (NO CALORIES vs CALORIES) rather than food cues versus a neutral/non-reward control stimulus; there is no qualifying cue>control within-subject contrast. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (food > non-food and high-calorie > low-calorie). The authors performed group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected with Monte Carlo simulations) and report significant voxelwise clusters and ROI results. Key methodological details are provided (3T scanner, BrainVoyager preprocessing, participant demographics/range, cue types), and voxelwise task-evoked results are available in the main text/results. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions, so it appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7), and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: there is no clear visual cue component. The cue modality is gustatory (beer flavor sprays) with an appetitive control (Gatorade); no visual drug-related cues were used as the primary stimulus. The study does meet I4 (within-participant contrast [beer > Gatorade]), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with small-volume/FWE-corrected ROI results), I6 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (participant demographics and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing I3 (lack of visual cue component).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual-penetration stimuli (natural reward-related cues) with an explicit within-participant contrast of PEN>BOD (sexual cue > control). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses are reported (flexible factorial, FWE-corrected thresholds; conjunction maps), and methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI, preprocessing with SPM8) are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural reward-related cues) presented as sexual vs. neutral backgrounds. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing sexual>neutral (main effect of background) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (FDR-corrected whole-brain analyses) with figures/tables described. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using erotic visual cues (natural reward) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates and SVC FWE corrections (satisfies I3, I5, I6). However, the paper does not present a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., erotic cues > neutral/other control stimuli). Analyses focus on parametric modulation of subjective value, delay-related and decision-related regressors and group × medication interactions rather than a simple within-subject cue>control contrast required by I4. MRI field strength is not explicitly reported in the provided text (I7 not fully met). Because not all required inclusion criteria are met (notably I4), the study must be excluded from the planned meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of a drug (GHB) assessing natural reward-related (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (erotic vs. neutral pictures). The paper reports within-participant voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., erotic>neutral under placebo; GHB/neutral > placebo/neutral) with whole-brain analyses (threshold p<.001, k>15) and ROI small-volume FWE-corrected results (p<.05). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text with introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and an explicit within-subject cue contrast (Food > Activities). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses are reported (peak threshold p<0.001 with cluster FWE correction) and cluster coordinates/tables/figures are described. The paradigm uses visual-only stimuli and reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software details. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (food [high+low-calorie] > nonfood; high-calorie > low-calorie; high-calorie > nonfood). These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual reward-related cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (soft-drink/brand cues) using visual stimuli (advertisements and logos). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of Coke product ads > non-food ads and Coke logo ads > non-food ads. Results are reported as group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistics with whole-brain cluster-wise FWE correction (pFWE < 0.05) and coordinates/tables are provided. Participant characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI cluster correction) are described. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts of food>control (HC–C, LC–C, HC–LC, Food–C) at the group level, analyzed with whole-brain voxelwise statistics in SPM8 with cluster correction (voxel p<0.001, cluster extent threshold derived from Monte Carlo simulation). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full-text fMRI study examines neural responses to visual infant face cues (natural rewards) in substance-using and non-using mothers and includes within-subject contrasts (own vs unknown infant faces, emotional expressions) that operationalize cue>control comparisons. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level results (voxel p<0.001, pFWE<0.05) and thus meet the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report participant demographics, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI drug/natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related and matched neutral pictures). The paradigm includes within-participant task conditions (craving, regulation, neutral) and contrasts such as craving versus neutral and regulation versus craving. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported (height threshold P<0.01 uncorrected with cluster-level FWE correction via AlphaSim; tables/figures and peak coordinates are provided), and additional gPPI connectivity analyses are presented. Key metadata are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual alcohol cues (pictures) with adult nondependent drinkers, directly addressing cue-reactivity. It includes a within-participant contrast of alcohol > neutral cues and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (voxel p<.001 combined with cluster p<.05 FWE), with coordinates and cluster descriptions provided. gPPI connectivity is reported in addition to task-evoked activations. Participant demographics and covariates (age, sex analyses) are reported; MRI protocol details are referenced and available in supplementary material. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise results. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and does not present a qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result (E3). The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses visual natural-reward cues: high- and low-calorie food images) and I4 (within-participant contrasts of high-calorie > low-calorie and related contrasts). Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise group-level result. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards). MRI field strength (3T), participant sex counts, cue type, and preprocessing/statistics details are provided. Therefore it meets I3 (natural reward visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise SVC results), I6 (coordinates/results reported), and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food pictures (natural reward cues) in children. MRI field strength (3.0T), participant age/sex, cue type, preprocessing and analysis software (AFNI, ANTs) and acquisition parameters are described. Full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study meets the review objective (fMRI cue-reactivity to natural reward visual stimuli) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural (food) reward cue-reactivity that uses clear visual cues (images signaling milkshake vs tasteless solution) and reports within-participant contrasts of cue>control (unpaired milkshake cue – unpaired tasteless cue). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food photographs). It includes within-participant contrasts (fattening food > objects; non-fattening food > objects) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses conducted within anatomically defined ROIs with cluster-thresholding (i.e., small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie and high-calorie > neutral) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked SPM results from a whole-brain analysis (voxel-level threshold P<0.001, clusters reported with coordinates), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise results. The paradigm used visual food images and the methods report MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual pornographic cues (pornographic vs neutral images) with within-participant contrasts (pornographic > neutral). Participant demographics, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are provided. MRI field strength is not explicitly stated in the provided text, but missing that detail alone does not exclude the study. Therefore the study meets criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food (animal) and food>blurred baseline images, and conducts group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM) with cluster-level whole-brain correction (alpha < .05). Coordinates and cluster locations are reported in the text (e.g., BA45, x,y,z), and methods report MRI field strength, preprocessing steps, and software (BrainVoyager). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical design).

This is an fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (pictures of high- and low-calorie foods) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > cars; high-calorie > low-calorie) reported. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and significance assessed using small-volume correction (SVC) within a priori ROIs (i.e., qualifying small-volume-corrected task-evoked results). The paper reports coordinates/ROIs, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistics software (SPM2), and participant demographics (age/sex/BMI). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of visual smoking cues with within-subject contrasts (smoke vs neutral) and sufficient methodological details (age range, cue type, 3T field strength, preprocessing/software). However, the paper reports individualized ROI selection and subsequent ROI-based analyses (percent signal change, ROI t-tests) and does not present a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical result (no qualifying group voxelwise maps or SVC-corrected results reported). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (group-level voxelwise result) and does not provide qualifying voxelwise results as per I6. Exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain/SVC result) applies, so the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using visual fractal cues predicting natural rewards (food). It includes within-participant contrasts of reward-predicting cues versus reward-omission cues (reward cue > omission cue) at the time of cue, and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-threshold corrected maps and tables/figures). Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are reported. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity and qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images vs matched object images. The study includes within-participant contrasts of food>object, reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results at the whole-brain level and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (permutation-based cluster correction), and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of food images > nonfood control images and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (activation t-maps, random-effects group maps with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction via Monte Carlo), presented in figures and described in the main text. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli (IAPS). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (food > neutral) at the subject level and subsequent group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM5), with results reported using whole-brain and ROI (FDR) correction and coordinate tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only, or non-empirical).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The study includes within-participant contrasts of food images > non-food images, reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster correction (Z>2.3, p<0.05), and provides coordinate tables and details of MRI field strength and preprocessing. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or absence of within-participant cue>control contrast) are met. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This manuscript is a study protocol describing planned fMRI assessments of visual food cues (natural reward) and detailed planned within-subject contrasts and voxelwise analyses, but it does not report any original human fMRI data or task-evoked voxelwise results (no results, coordinates, or group-level analyses presented). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/protocol without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI study targeting natural reward visual cues) is met based on design. However I4 (at least one actual within-participant cue>control analysis reported) and I5 (at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result reported as whole-brain or SVC) are not met because no empirical results are presented. As a result, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural (social/sexual) reward-related cue-reactivity using visual cues (anticipatory cues for male/female smiling faces vs control dysmorphed stimuli). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (visual natural reward cues: face cues), I4 (within-participant contrasts of reward cue > control and analyses of anticipation-related activation), I5 (group-level voxelwise results reported: whole-brain analyses thresholded at p<0.05 FWE and small-volume-corrected ROI results for VTA/NAcc/vmPFC), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/tables), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software reported). This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Participants viewed visual high- and low-calorie food pictures and control images; within-subject contrasts (HC–C, LC–C, HC–LC, LC–HC) are reported. Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted (2×2 repeated measures ANOVA) with ROI-based small-volume correction (p<=0.05 FWE/SVC) and coordinates/clusters are reported. Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that used visual (pictorial) cues (multimodal visual+auditory, with visual component). Analyses include within-participant contrasts (high- and low-calorie food cues and comparisons to neutral non-foods; relative high>low contrasts were used in regressions), reported as group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain cluster-extent correction (P<0.05 corrected via Monte Carlo/AlphaSim) and with coordinates/statistical maps described. Participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cues using visual stimuli and includes a within-participant contrast (fattening vs. non-fattening food cues) and reports MRI field strength and preprocessing details (I3, I4, I7 met). However, the reported fMRI results are based on an ROI-approach with averaged activation across predefined ROIs and region-by-region ROI analyses; the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results or coordinate tables for a qualifying voxelwise contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete. Excluded for not reporting qualifying voxelwise group-level results (see E3).

This is an empirical fMRI study of conditioning to drug-paired cues using compound audiovisual stimuli that include a clear visual component. The design uses a within-subjects contrast comparing methamphetamine-paired versus placebo-paired cues, and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (AFNI 3dmvm, cluster-corrected results reported in Table 3 and Fig. 2). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, 3.0T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses perfusion fMRI with audio/visual smoking cues and matched non-smoking control stimuli, employing within-subject SC>non-SC contrasts at the group level. Voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed within an a priori ROI mask (including dorsal striatum/putamen), with reported voxelwise t-statistics and significance thresholds (p<0.005, cluster≥20) and an explicit report of a left putamen effect (t=2.77). These constitute qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results within an ROI (small-volume) framework. Participant sex, cue type, imaging modality and analysis software are described or referenced. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the paper meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI visual drug-cue reactivity and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images (meets I3). The authors report within-participant contrasts of food>neutral images (food–neutral image contrast) used in group analyses (meets I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using small-volume-corrected ROI analyses with FWE-correction and multivariate voxelwise PLS results reported with cluster/peak statistics (meets I5 and I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, PLS) are reported (meets I7). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy volunteers that uses clear visual cues (chocolate picture and mouldy drink) paired with tastes, fulfilling cue-reactivity with a visual component. The paper reports within-participant cue>control contrasts (e.g. pleasant/unpleasant cue vs grey image) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with whole-brain cluster correction and small-volume FWE corrections for a priori ROIs; coordinates and peak activations are reported in tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is original human fMRI data). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol-picture stimuli in adolescents. It includes a within-subject contrast of alcohol pictures > non-alcohol beverage pictures, reports group-level voxelwise statistical analyses both within a priori ROIs (small-volume/ROI-constrained voxelwise tests with cluster correction via AlphaSim) and an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis (3dttest++ with cluster correction). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Excluded under E3. The study uses visual smoking cues and reports a within-participant smoking>nonsmoking contrast (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the provided full text presents ROI-based task-evoked results (parameter estimates extracted from a priori ROIs) and regression/mediation analyses on those ROI values, and does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables in the main text (I5 not met). Full text appears complete (no evidence of truncation). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported).

This is an empirical fMRI study of appetitive (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual erotic stimuli and visual conditioned cues. The study reports within-participant contrasts (CS+ > CS− and erotic pictures > control) at the group level, with voxelwise whole-brain results and ROI small-volume-corrected (FWE) results, and provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food pictures. The study used within-subject contrasts comparing food versus neutral object conditions (food>neutral), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (RFX ANOVA F-maps and conjunction t-contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster criteria. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (high/low calorie food images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX v1.9) are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (F, t, and r maps), uses voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo simulation), and presents regional results and associations with BMI. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) with clear visual cues and group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results, it does NOT include a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food images > neutral/control stimuli). This is an empirical high-resolution fMRI study using visual fractal cues predicting natural reward (juice) and neutral/aversive outcomes. This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual infant-face stimuli (natural rewards) with within-subject contrasts (own-happy vs unknown-happy; own-sad vs unknown-sad). Participant demographics, MRI acquisition (3T), preprocessing, and analysis software (BrainVoyager) are described. Thus the study provides a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise within-participant natural reward>control contrast using visual cues, meeting the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. Although this is an fMRI study using visual natural reward (food) cues and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with peak coordinates, it does not present a qualifying within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control (e.g., food > non-food) in the reported results. This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (food words). This is an empirical RCT reporting mindfulness training effects with resting-state fMRI, DTI, and behavioral measures of craving/smoking, but it does not report a task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural reward cues nor report a within-participant cue>control contrast. This study is an fMRI experiment measuring alcohol cue reactivity using visual images and reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > pleasant). This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.
