The study is an empirical fMRI task study using visual natural reward cues (food photographs) and reports within-participant contrasts between food and non-food stimuli during fMRI. Methods state that whole-brain voxel-wise random-effects group analyses were performed (with multiple-comparison correction) and report region-level results and associations, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant ages/sex and cue type are reported; although MRI field strength and full preprocessing/software details are not explicit in the excerpt, missing such preferred details alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (only ROI analyses, connectivity/resting-state-only, absence of within-participant cue>control contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using a multimodal (visual cue words + taste delivery) Alcohol Taste > Water Taste within-participant contrast. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with tables and figures. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T Siemens Prisma), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, ICA-AROMA), and task/cue details. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, original human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual cues (milkshake vs. water images) and within-participant contrasts of cue>control (milkshake picture > water picture) and taste>control. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (cluster sizes, p-values, Z-scores) using FSL FEAT, satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise task-evoked result. Participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

While this fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control (neutral) stimuli as required by I4. The reported contrasts are choices versus rejects (both involving food cues) and attention-condition comparisons (HD vs ND, TD vs ND), but ND is an attentional/control instruction rather than a non-food or neutral stimulus control contrast typical of cue-reactivity designs. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (coordinates/figures reported), I7 (participant demographics and MRI details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control stimulus contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply based on the full text.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (palatable, neutral) with within-participant contrasts (palatable > neutral items) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected), reporting coordinates and preprocessing details. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual food cues (natural reward) in a within-subject crossover design. It reports a within-participant contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie food images and provides a group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected result in the hypothalamus (one voxel survives SVC, p=0.0125). An exploratory whole-brain analysis was also conducted (FWE-corrected). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (chocolate) cue reactivity that includes visual stimuli (chocolate pictures) during scanning. The authors report within-participant contrasts of chocolate>neutral pictures and group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical analyses (2-way and 3-way ANOVAs), with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables/figures providing Talairach coordinates for significant clusters. MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing software (BrainVoyager QX), and participant demographics (female, healthy-weight; age reported in Table 1) are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is a task-evoked fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food images) with within-subject food>nonfood contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPM8), including corrected whole-brain results and coordinates, and also ROI analyses. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply. Although sample size is small (n=9), this does not violate inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (side-by-side images of high-calorie, low-calorie, and non-food). It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie vs. non-food (cue>control) in pre- and post-meal states. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using whole-brain cluster-based correction (Monte Carlo simulations) with Talairach coordinates and tables/figures of activations. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing and statistical software (BrainVoyager), and participant demographic information (age, sex). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical design). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of sexual>neutral cues (subliminal and supraliminal), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (tables/coordinates and figures). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistics software (SPM5), participant age/sex, and stimulus/cue details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study does not assess cue-reactivity to drug-related or natural reward visual cues. It uses the monetary incentive delay task to measure reward anticipation (nondrug monetary rewards) rather than a within-participant cue>control contrast involving drug or natural reward visual cues. Therefore it fails to meet I3 (study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast of drug or natural reward cues). It does meet several methodological criteria relevant to the review (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction and reported peak coordinates, and reporting of participant/MRI details), but because I3 and I4 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of resting cerebral blood flow 4 h after high- vs low-GI meals and does not involve presentation of visual reward or drug-related cues or a within-participant cue>control task contrast. It therefore fails key inclusion criteria for a cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Specifically, the study lacks any visual cue component and does not report a within-participant cue>control task-evoked contrast; although it reports group-level voxelwise results (with coordinates) and provides participant age/sex and MRI details, these do not satisfy the required task-evoked cue-reactivity design. Thus it is not eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study using visual cocaine cues (images of cocaine and paraphernalia) and includes a within-participant cocaine>neutral contrast at first-level and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (cluster-level whole-brain thresholding in SPM8) reporting significant clusters (e.g., putamen, insula, occipital cortex). MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8), participant age range and sex composition (men and women, 18–65), and cue type are reported. Results are presented as task-evoked group-level voxelwise findings. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study using the monetary incentive delay task with clear visual incentive cues (symbols indicating monetary amounts). It includes within-participant cue>control contrasts (gain cues > ¥0) and reports group-level voxelwise statistical results, including small-volume FWE-corrected ROI analysis in nucleus accumbens, satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual monetary incentive cues (monetary incentive delay task) with within-participant contrasts of anticipation of gain vs neutral and loss vs neutral. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed with small-volume correction in the ventral striatum and results reported with FWE-corrected coordinates. The full text includes methods (MRI field strength, preprocessing, software), participant demographics, task/cue type, and results. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual picture stimuli with a within-subject alcohol>neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-test and regression), provides peak coordinates and used cluster-level FWE correction, and includes relevant task and participant information. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and required voxelwise reporting criteria.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (beer bottle images). The paradigm modeled Go (coke/water) and NoGo (beer) trials separately and generated first-level contrast images which were entered into second-level (random effects) voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported (SPM8, p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster threshold/AlphaSim), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise evidence. Thus the paper provides a within-participant contrast involving alcohol cues versus control stimuli (beer NoGo vs non-alcohol Go/baseline) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results. Participant/sample, cue type, field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore all core inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because it reports only ROI-based voxel-averaged results rather than any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical maps, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related visual food cues), I4 (within-participant food>non-food contrast), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (geometric cues in the Monetary Incentive Delay task) to probe natural reward (monetary) anticipation. The paper reports within-participant cue contrasts (gain anticipation: +¥20/+¥100/+¥500 > ¥0) and group-level voxelwise analyses, including whole-brain cluster results and an a priori small-volume (NAc) ROI with FWE-corrected statistics. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/MATLAB) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task fMRI study of monetary (natural) reward cue-reactivity using a visual cue-based MID-R task. It reports within-participant contrasts (gain-neutral and loss-neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses with small-volume correction in predefined ROIs; results are described in the main text and figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing, and analysis software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (participant-selected food images). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing food vs. non-food (viewing food–viewing non-food and distraction food–distraction non-food). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain FWE cluster-corrected thresholds (p<0.05) and cluster coordinates/voxel counts, satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Relevant methodological details (participant demographics/sex, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8) are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper). This article is a commentary/systematic review of stimuli used in alcohol cue-reactivity neuroimaging studies and does not present original human fMRI data or any task-evoked voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an original functional MRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported from original data), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6/I7 not applicable because no original voxelwise results exist. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and multiple other picture categories. It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral and other category > neutral), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction; results are presented in figures and tables with Talairach coordinates. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager QX), and participant sample details are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual cues (written cue words) and visual stimuli (pictures/videos), meeting the review topic. It reports within-participant contrasts CUE SEM – CUE NEUTRAL and SEM – NEUTRAL. Group-level voxelwise results are reported: ROI analyses with SPM small-volume correction (FWE) and explorative whole-brain FWE-corrected analyses. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, Matlab) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-induced desire for an Internet video game (a natural reward) using visual-only stimuli (450-s videotape without sound). It reports within-subject contrasts of video-game cues > neutral stimuli and group-level random-effects voxelwise results with whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (FDR) and Talairach coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task using visual-only stimuli (alcohol vs neutral images) with a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the alcohol>neutral contrast are reported (significant activations in mOFC, occipital cortex, PCC; thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction described). Participant demographics and scanning/preprocessing details are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (the paper includes task-evoked whole-brain results, not only ROI/connectivity or between-group-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not contain a task-evoked cue-reactivity fMRI contrast. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI cue-reactivity assessment; visual food cues were shown after scanning, not during fMRI), I4 (no within-participant cue>control task contrast in the fMRI data), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise task results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in heavy drinkers using visual cues (images signaling alcohol, food, neutral) in the AFID task. The paper reports within-subject image-type analyses (e.g., alcohol > neutral and alcohol > food) during the anticipatory phase, and group-level voxelwise analyses across the whole brain as well as ROI (small-volume) analyses with cluster thresholds and reported coordinates. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing software (AFNI), and other participant details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water), with within-participant contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation, outcome notification, and delivery phases. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (T-maps thresholded voxel-wise p<.001 and cluster-level FWE p<.05) and provides coordinates/figures/supplementary tables. Participant demographics (age, male-only), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, FSL ICA-AROMA) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This paper reports an fMRI task using visual smoking cues (BEGIN and END pictures) and matched visual control pictures, meeting the visual cue requirement. Within-subject contrasts (smoking > control) were computed at first level and carried to group-level second analyses, satisfying the cue>control contrast requirement. Group-level voxelwise results are reported using anatomically defined ROI masks with voxelwise FWE-correction (i.e., small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical results), meeting the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected evidence. Results are presented in the main text (tables/figures referenced). Participant/task/MRI details and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E3 met: the manuscript reports cue-reactivity results using ROI extractions (NAcc percent-signal-change) and ROI-based functional connectivity estimates, but does not present a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) for the cue>neutral contrasts that would qualify for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue reactivity task with alcohol/appetitive/neutral images), I4 (within-participant contrasts such as alcohol>neutral and appetitive>neutral were computed and used), and I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result for the cue-reactivity contrasts is reported). Therefore the study must be excluded from the cue-reactivity coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol (drug-related) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (advertisement images). It reports a within-participant contrast (ALCOHOL > CONTROL) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical results (cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates in tables/figures). Methods report participant age/sex, 3.0T MRI field strength, preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8), and detailed acquisition/analysis parameters. Results include whole-brain activations and coordinate tables as well as ROI analyses; therefore the study satisfies the review’s requirements for voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This report is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (e-cigarette advertisements) vs matched neutral advertisements in adolescents, with within-subject contrasts (e-cigarette > neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported and cluster-corrected. Methods report participant ages/sex, 3T scanner, and AFNI preprocessing/statistics. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3–I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures vs. non-food). It contains within-participant contrasts (food>non-food; high-calorie>non-food) at the first level and reports group-level voxelwise second-level regression analyses. Results include small-volume-corrected (SVC) voxelwise in a priori ROIs with FWE correction, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. The paper reports participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual images of appetizing, disgusting, bland foods and nonfood objects to probe neural responses to food cues (natural rewards). It includes within-subject contrasts of appetizing>bland and appetizing>nonfood, published group-level random-effects voxelwise results with reported coordinates, and small-volume-corrected (SVC) statistics for a priori ROIs. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplemental materials are not required). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity natural reward fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food (natural reward) cues and body-image cues. It includes within-participant contrasts of food>low-level baseline (and food>non-food) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with Talairach coordinates and cluster analyses. MRI field strength (1.5T), participant sex/characteristics, cue types, and analysis software (XBAM) are reported. The full text contains background, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise cue-reactivity with visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (erotic and monetary pictures) with within-subject contrasts (high vs low erotic/monetary; outcome vs anticipation) and pharmacological challenge. It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume-corrected p-values in predefined ROIs (ventral striatum, OFC, amygdala, hypothalamus, mPFC) and provides figures/tables of activations, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise or SVC-corrected results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, DARTEL, Ledalab) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper contains original fMRI data acquired with visual food cues and reports voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected coordinates) using AFNI and a 3T scanner, and reports participant age/sex and cue type. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural-reward food cues), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise, cluster-corrected results reported with coordinates), I6 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures), and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). However, the manuscript does not report a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food>non-food) as a qualifying analysis; the group results focus on high-ED vs low-ED food image contrasts (food vs food), not cue>control. Because I4 (at least one within-participant cue>control contrast) is not satisfied, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the paper.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of candy/dessert). It uses a within-subject design and reports within-participant contrasts of food-picture conditions relative to low-level baseline and regulation contrasts (LATER vs NOW). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain FWE-corrected statistics and MNI coordinates, and a small-volume (ROI) analysis is also reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) appears present. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of smoking-related (drug) cue-reactivity using pictorial visual stimuli and reports a within-subject contrast of smoking versus neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported and thresholded using small-volume FWE correction in a priori ROIs (ACC, DLPFC, SPL), satisfying the requirement for small-volume-corrected voxelwise evidence. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (pictorial), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with a within-participant contrast of food>nonfood images. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected via Monte Carlo) and provides coordinates and supplemental whole-brain maps, and also reports small-volume/ROI analyses for the nucleus accumbens. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies with qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual alcohol images (I3 met). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (condition > fixation) are reported and cluster-corrected (whole-brain), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise results (I5, I6). Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing and analysis software are reported (I7). However, the manuscript does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., respond alcohol > respond neutral); the authors explicitly state that direct comparisons of the two response conditions were not conducted because the design did not allow a clean contrast, so inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I4 is missing, the study must be excluded.

Full text is unavailable (provided content is a redirect/interstitial page, not the article). Cannot verify required inclusion criteria for the review objective. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3-E6 cannot be assessed). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met / not verifiable: I3 (unclear whether this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study with visual cues), I4 (no evidence of a within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no confirmation of group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results), I6 (no confirmation that voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement), I7 (cannot confirm reporting of participant/method details). Because the full text is incomplete, the study cannot be confirmed to satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria; exclude pending availability of the complete article for re-screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food pictures) and within-subject contrasts (food > nonfood; high-calorie food > nonfood). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with family-wise error small-volume correction within predefined ROIs; results are presented in figures and supplementary table. MRI field strength (3.0 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (photographs) of a natural reward (romantic partner) with a within-participant contrast (rejecter > neutral). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: ROI-based small-volume-corrected analyses (sphere ROIs, FDR-corrected) with coordinates and cluster details in tables, and unpredicted regions thresholded at p<0.001 with cluster information. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Although whole-brain corrected results were not significant, the presence of small-volume-corrected ROI voxelwise group results satisfies the requirement for a qualifying task-evoked statistical result.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (high- and low-calorie food images) with within-participant contrasts (HCF vs NF, LCF vs NF). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported and FWE-corrected (AFNI AlphaSim), with results presented in text, figures, and supplementary tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (BioImageSuite, AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original fMRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study of natural (food) reward-related cue processing using clear visual cues (graphical basket/wallet cues in the food and monetary incentive delay tasks), and includes within-participant contrasts of high-reward vs no-reward (10 SP vs 0 SP; 1 EUR vs 0 EUR) for both anticipation and receipt phases. Group-level voxelwise results are reported: small-volume-corrected ROI results (FWE P<0.05) and whole-brain cluster-corrected results (P<0.05 cluster-level, voxel threshold P<0.001), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Relevant methodological details (participant demographics, cue types, 3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing/analysis) are provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a natural reward (food) that used visual cue stimuli (images of marzipan objects) and a within-participant contrast (CS+ > CS-) at the group level. The paper reports voxelwise analyses including whole-brain results (p<.001 uncorrected) and small-volume-corrected (SVC) cluster-level FWE-corrected findings in left caudate and right amygdala, fulfilling the requirement for qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food and non-food pictures). The design includes within-subject contrasts (post-load vs. baseline responses to food pictures and separate modeling of high vs. low caloric food blocks; task includes non-food control blocks), and group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with tables/coordinates and figures. Multiple regression results are reported with multiple-comparison correction. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines alcohol cue-reactivity using gustatory (taste) cues rather than visual cues, so it does not meet I3 (requires a clear visual cue component). It does meet I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5 (voxelwise task-evoked results with ROI/small-volume approaches and reported peak coordinates), I6 (results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (reports participant demographics and imaging details). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue‑reactivity using visual picture stimuli (social and non‑social alcohol and soda images). It includes within‑participant contrasts (e.g., alcohol vs soda and interaction (SA>SS)-(NA>NS)), and reports group‑level voxelwise whole‑brain results with coordinates and cluster‑level FWE correction. Participant demographic and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are provided. Thus it satisfies the meta‑analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI‑only, not connectivity/resting‑state only, and includes within‑subject cue>control contrasts). The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation with within-subject alcohol taste > control taste contrasts and group-level voxelwise results, but the primary cue modality is gustatory (taste) rather than visual. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (with a priori ROI small-volume approaches and coordinate tables/figures), participant demographics, MRI field strength (3-T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). However, the meta-analysis requires a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual cues). This study used taste delivery accompanied by visual instructions, but the alcohol cue itself was gustatory; thus I3 is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images) and includes within-subject contrasts of food>neutral. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (2×3 ANOVA and food>neutral contrasts) with multiple-comparison correction (FWE via AlphaSim), and results are reported at the whole-brain level. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM5, BioImageSuite, AFNI) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI/TMS study that measures TMS-evoked BOLD responses before and after cTBS in cocaine- and alcohol-dependent individuals; it is not a visual cue-reactivity fMRI task. (a) Exclusion criterion met: E5 — the study does not include any within-participant drug-cue > control visual cue contrast required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 — the paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked (TMS-evoked) whole-brain results (FDR-corrected clusters); I6 — voxelwise results are reported in supplementary tables/figures; I7 — reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — the study does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component (it uses recall/imagery and TMS-evoked BOLD, not visual cue exposure); I4 — there is no within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli. Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This study used resting-state and pre/post ingestion fMRI (ALFF and seed-based functional connectivity) to examine responses to actual yogurt ingestion and the effect of verbal fat labels. It did not present any visual cue-based reward or drug cue paradigm, nor a within-participant task-evoked cue>control contrast using visual stimuli. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), or I5 (qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). It does report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (satisfied I7). It reports voxelwise resting-state results but these are not task-evoked cue-reactivity results, so exclusion criterion E4 (only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without task-evoked voxelwise results) applies. Full text appears complete.
